382YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: The Senate faced assigning newly conquered Ossium, which has virtually no native Imperial citizens. Morrow could be evacuated, though at least a fifth of its people would be left behind, and an alternative was proposed. Nearly two thousand slaves freed at Dubhtraig, mostly orcs, needed new homes, and another raid on Beoraidh was offered. The Navarr had a fleeting chance to reclaim Westwood while the vallorn surged in Brocéliande. Frederick di Sarvos offered to build one of four university projects. Gilah consecrated the Kraken's Bane in Calvos Sound as an inspirational memorial. Sixteen mandates were upheld, many urging nations to support Highborn pilgrims. New rituals and Druj-derived potions entered Imperial lore.

n.Dawn: Dawnish armies were hailed for victories at Semmerholm, Weirwater and Ossium, and Pelleas Thorne's mandate opened new chances to capitalise on them. The troubadours named Ser Isidore Ossienne and Lord Colwyn de Rondel as champions of Love and Glory, and Dawn was urged to aid pilgrims and perhaps Brocéliande.
n.Druj: The Druj were defeated in Ossium, the Empire's first new conquest in decades, and potions were translated from a captured Druj herbal. Their threat still loomed over Morrow and enslaved Zenith.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost nearly two thousand slaves freed at Dubhtraig. An opportunity arose to raid the sinking city of Beoraidh and free an army of orc gladiators who hate the Salt Lords.
n.Highguard: Highguard's renewal continued as nine nations' mandates spread support for its pilgrims, and Able of the Shattered Tower called for a revival of the missionary tradition. Rebuilding the Lepidean Library in Bastion was one of four architectural proposals.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were the obvious home for the slaves freed from the Grendel, and the Winter Sun general was urged towards a raid on Beoraidh. Skywise Tulva's mandate called on orc citizens to support the pilgrims.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a conjunction to battle the Jotun in Sermersuaq was listed among the season's opportunities.
n.Navarr: The Navarr had a closing window to reclaim Westwood from a weakened vallorn while struggling to hold back its surge in Brocéliande. Corey Brackensong's mandate costs every Navarr herb garden two random herbs each season until Winter 383YE.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast was named as a possible home for freed orc slaves and gained an inspirational memorial at the Kraken's Bane, with a chance to build a Prosperity seminary. A new school in Siroc was also proposed.
n.The League: Expanding Holberg University and renovating Diora University in Sarvos were among Frederick di Sarvos's proposals. The League was also floated as a home for freed orc slaves and pledged support for the pilgrims.
n.The Marches: Marcher generals were celebrated, with children named after them, and Friar John of the Mourn's mandate pushed the yeomen to adapt Marcher ways of war to their heritage. Hrodin's mandate called on Marchers to aid the pilgrims.
n.Urizen: Urizen weighed evacuating Morrow, which would leave a fifth of its people behind, against a proposal to bring light back after the loss of the Halls of Knowledge. Further opportunities were offered against a curse rotting its food.
n.Varushka: Slaves were freed in Varushka amid looming territorial disputes with orcs. Father Drakov's mandate urged Varushkans to support the pilgrims.
n.Wintermark: Gunnbrand Ironwill's mandate turned Wintermark armies against the use of envenomed blades on anyone but the vallorn, and Rane Sherarding's mandate spread the burden of supporting pilgrims to Wintermark.

t.Bastion: Rebuilding Bastion's Lepidean Library was one of four proposals awaiting a decision by the Senate or a wayleave holder.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: fleets on the Bay of Catazar were tagged in the orc affairs entry, which hinted at bloodthirsty pirates and a silent armada.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn of Brocéliande stirred, sending ettercaps and vallornspawn against steadings the Navarr spent centuries liberating. A conjunction to fight it there was also identified.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: residents of Feroz were tagged in the winds of magic entry.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the northern Feni left Hahnmark and crossed into Hercynia.
t.Hercynia: The northern Feni arrived in Hercynia from Hahnmark and showed no sign of vanishing peacefully into the forest.
t.Holberg: Expanding Holberg University was proposed as one of Frederick di Sarvos's four projects, and Holberg's residents were tagged in the winds of magic.
t.Liathaven: The weakened vallorn of western Liathaven gave the Navarr a short-lived chance of victory, while the Feni of the Woods that Fell disappeared into the forest.
t.Madruga: The Kraken's Bane in Madruga was consecrated as an inspirational memorial, raising the chance of a Prosperity seminary for Imperial and Sumaash pilgrims.
t.Morrow: The civil service judged that Morrow could be evacuated, though at least a fifth of its people would be left behind, and a rival proposal sought to restore hope. A conjunction to free slaves there was also identified.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher generals were praised for having liberated the Mournwold.
t.Ossium: With Ossium conquered from the Druj and almost no native Imperial citizens, the Senate had to choose which of the ten nations should receive it. A conjunction to delve into its woods was also identified.
t.Redoubt: A conjunction was identified to challenge orc opportunists in Redoubt.
t.Sarvos: Renovating Diora University in Sarvos was one of the four proposals, and Sarvos residents were tagged in the winds of magic.
t.Semmerholm: Dawn had driven the Druj from Semmerholm, and a conjunction offered a chance to end the Eater-of-Hope, which had run to ground there.
t.Sermersuaq: A conjunction was identified to battle the Jotun in Sermersuaq.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel in Spiral was recalled as one of Urizen's recent losses.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: residents of Temeschwar were tagged in the winds of magic entry.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish armies crossed the Semmerlak with the aid of Summer eternals to surprise the Druj in Ossium.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish armies were credited with crushing the unliving horrors assailing Weirwater.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the people of Zenith were described as enslaved by the Druj, and its residents were tagged in the winds of magic.

r.Liathaven/Westwood: The Navarr had a fleeting chance to reclaim Westwood from the vallorn and reunite north and south for the first time since Terunael fell.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Gilah used true liao to consecrate the Kraken's Bane at its dry dock in Calvos Sound as an inspirational memorial, raising the chance to build a Prosperity seminary there.

382YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: Around 250 fleets and 300 warbands raided Tathar and sacked Dubhtraig. They gutted half its shipyard, ruined Salt Lord Suriad's palace and freed up to two thousand slaves. Lasambrian Jotun seized Anduzjasse, raided across Segura, exiled Freeborn who refused them, and offered peace only for Segura and Feroz. The Drakes destroyed the Feni settlement inside a Winter regio in Alderly but were cursed. At a crystal-transformed Canterspire, six Imperial armies drove the Druj from Operus. Wintermark-led armies retook nine-tenths of Sealtoq but not Atalaq. Dawnish and Varushkan armies, aided by the Thule and Summer knights, conquered Echofell and Webwood. That made Ossium the first new territory in two centuries.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights spearheaded the breach of Suriad's palace and a Dawnish-Winterfolk fleet burned the weirwood ships of Balsagoth. Four Dawnish armies took the Tower of the Scorpion and conquered Echofell and Webwood in Ossium.
n.Druj: The Druj were turned back at Canterspire and lost Operus, and they were harried in Peregro and Caeli. In Ossium the Amber Scorpion lost their tower and thousands of orcs, and the survivors retreated into the southern forests.
n.Grendel: Dubhtraig was sacked, its shipyard more than half gutted and Suriad's palace left in ruins, with rumours that the Salt Lord fell. No navy can be built there for a year, and the Fort Fuil and Fort Salann garrisons were badly depleted.
n.Highguard: Highborn soldiers held Dubhtraig's western docks, and the burning beasts of Jachin's Legacy broke the palace gates. Highborn armies savaged in Morrow had already withdrawn to Astolat and Casinea.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc warbands rallied enslaved orcs at Dubhtraig and fought in its mines, though Spring magic made some dangerously aggressive while they waited. The Winter Sun joined the steady conquest of Sealtoq.
n.Jotun: Lasambrian Jotun under the firebird banner conquered Anduzjasse, pressed into Anozeseri and offered terms for Segura and Feroz. In Sermersuaq the Jotun lost most of Sealtoq but held Atalaq, and Yrsa Jansdóttir is enraged by the destruction of the truce stone.
n.Navarr: Navarr runners carried the signal to sail and Navarr soldiers seized Dubhtraig's towers. The Black Thorns fought honourably in Sealtoq and the Quiet Step escorted the Feni exiles into Liathaven.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn lost Anduzjasse and saw raids across Segura, with penniless exiles fleeing east and southern trade choked off, and the Lasambrians now threaten Feroz. Freeborn corsairs blockaded Dubhtraig, and the Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs fought in Sermersuaq.
n.The League: League bravos excelled in Dubhtraig's streets while Sarvos stayed quiet under the watch of the Grendel armada. The Towerjacks and Wolves of War helped break the Druj at Canterspire.
n.The Marches: The Drakes destroyed the Feni village in Alderly, at the cost of 120 casualties, the deaths of Alderly Marchers who sided with the Feni, and a curse. Marcher soldiers guarded Dubhtraig's docks, and the Tusks and Bounders fought in Sealtoq.
n.Thule: Allied with the Military Council, the Thule conquered the Bonewood with rumoured heavy losses. They then delivered about 150 Imperial slaves freed from the Druj.
n.Urizen: Canterspire became a crystal citadel guarded by Phaleron's heralds, and the Druj were driven from Operus. However, Naeve's Twisting Blight lies over Morrow, Redoubt and Spiral, and the people of the Arbiter's Seat chose Kaela's gift.
n.Varushka: The Iron Helms and Northern Eagle fought at Canterspire, and the Golden Axe helped conquer Echofell and Webwood. Varushkans also seized towers and fought in the mines at Dubhtraig.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's three armies, Winterfolk heroes and Summer knights led the retaking of nine-tenths of Sealtoq, though Atalaq remains Jotun. A few Suaq have taken the Choice and become Jotun.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Highborn armies withdrew to Astolat from Morrow, and the Tusks' Summer allies marched from there.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: home of several captains in the Dubhtraig raid, including members of Jachin's Legacy.
t.Bay of Catazar: The armada gathered at ports all along the Bay and crossed it to Tathar, dominating the waters off the Broken Shore during the raid.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: home of some Marcher captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Highborn armies savaged in Morrow withdrew westward to Casinea.
t.Feroz: The Lasambrian Jotun declared that Feroz is their next target after Segura. For now the eastern trade route through Bramar remains open.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: home of many Winterfolk captains in the Dubhtraig raid, and the armies marched north through it.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: home of some Navarr captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: League bravos raised on Holberg's walls fought in Dubhtraig's streets.
t.Kahraman: Earlier in the year the Jotun seized Damata before being driven out. The Lasambrians now threaten to help Narkyst reclaim Kahraman if the Empire rejects their offer.
t.Kallavesa: Wintermark's three armies gathered around Rundhal, joined by ten thousand Summer knights and the Fire of the South, before marching north. Jotun warbands had been raiding its north.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders from Karov fought with the League armies at Canterspire.
t.Karsk: The Thule crossed from Karsk into the Bonewood. Moresvah families sent wagon raiders with mining supplies to the mithril mine at Lormaa.
t.Liathaven: The Feni of the Woods-that-Fell were ushered into Liaven's Glen, where Alderly's fleeing Feni also vanished. The Quiet Step is preparing an assault on Westwood.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: named among the lands the Lasambrians threaten to help Narkyst reclaim.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: home of some Navarr captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: home of some Varushkan captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: home of some Marcher captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Morrow: Six Imperial armies broke the Druj before a crystal-clad Canterspire and drove them from Operus into retreat in Caeli. The territory suffers Naeve's Twisting Blight, and the Arbiter's Seat lost its whole population to Kaela's gift.
t.Mournwold: Three armies passed through to deal with the Feni. The Drakes destroyed the hidden Feni village of Alderly while the other two escorted the Woods-that-Fell exiles out of the territory.
t.Necropolis: Burning stone beasts of Jachin's Legacy stood as living beacons on the docks of Sanctuary Sands, causing several small fires on the Necropolis quayside.
t.Ossium: The Empire conquered Echofell and Webwood and took the Tower of the Scorpion, holding four regions and the majority of the territory. The Senate may now assign it to a nation, though the Thule hold the Bonewood and the Druj still hold the south.
t.Redoubt: Naeve's Twisting Blight was reported to have been laid over Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: home of some Highborn captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: last winter the Jotun tried to smooth the passage from Reinos into Segura.
t.Sarvos: With the ransomed Grendel armada idling offshore, Sarvos kept up appearances while its ships slipped away to join the raid. Watchers then saw the Grendel admirals keep to the agreement after news of the attack arrived.
t.Segura: Lasambrian Jotun conquered Anduzjasse, seized seven Towers of Anduz and raided farms across the territory. They are also driving out Freeborn who refuse them and barring southern traders.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: home of some Dawnish captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Sermersuaq: Nine Imperial armies with Summer allies drove four Jotun armies and their reinforcements back to the walls of Atalaq, retaking most of Sealtoq. The Spring-infused waters healed both sides.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Jotun warbands had raided western Skarsind, and the Winter Sun's general spoke of one day returning home there.
t.Spiral: Naeve's Twisting Blight was reported to have been brought to bear in Spiral.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: League bravos raised in Tassato's alleys fought in Dubhtraig.
t.Tathar: Imperial raiders burned ports and supply lines, freed slaves and sacked Dubhtraig. The garrisons of Fort Fuil and Fort Salann suffered significant losses.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: bravos from Temeschwar's backstreets fought in Dubhtraig, and Temeschwari mercenaries marched with the League armies in Morrow.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's gift of painless death to captured Imperials extends into the Barrens.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: home of some Navarr captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Tsirku: Mentioned in passing: the reclaimed land is described as tiny beside the plains stretching towards the wasteland of Tsirku.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns marched north from distant Upwold.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders from Volodmartz fought with the League armies at Canterspire.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: home of some Dawnish captains listed in the Dubhtraig raid.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: recalled as where the Druj invasion began, and Kaela's gift extends there.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: not named; the page refers only generally to Brass Coast ports along the Bay of Catazar gathering ships for the raid.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: not named; Feroz as a whole is threatened by the Lasambrians.
r.Hahnmark/Bruckland: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark armies marched through Bruckland on their way into Sermersuaq.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Mentioned in passing: earlier in the year the Fort Braydon garrison stopped the Jotun pushing into Serra Briante.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Mentioned in passing: recalled as where the Jotun seized Damata after the Spring Equinox before being driven back.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: Mentioned in passing: the armies marched north through Skymark.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South left its camp on the edges of the Wittal Grove to join the Wintermark armies.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The Thule crossed from Krevsaty into the Bonewood. A Thule warband later marched south from Krevsaty to hand over about 150 Imperials freed from the Druj.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The three families of Moresvah hired wagon raiders to carry mining supplies to Lormaa, seeking to work its mithril mine with former Druj mine-slaves.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: The Feni exiles of the Woods-that-Fell were ushered into Liaven's Glen. A raven-masked figure later led a ragged band of Alderly Feni into its depths.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step's general says their assault on Westwood draws closer.
r.Morrow/Caeli: Imperial armies pushed into Caeli and liberated the Arbiter's Seat, only to find its people had all chosen death through Kaela's gift. A conjunction to Arbiter's Green has opened here.
r.Morrow/Operus: The Druj consolidated in Operus before Canterspire, then were pushed out entirely by the Imperial armies.
r.Morrow/Peregro: The Druj camped in Peregro after the Autumn Equinox and were later harried there by Imperial forces.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The Drakes followed secret paths into a Winter regio and destroyed the Feni village and its great oak, fighting Marcher locals who had joined the Feni. They emerged cursed.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Feni exiles were escorted down from the Chalkdowns, and the Drakes camped on its western edge before entering Alderly.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Mentioned in passing: fleeing Alderly Feni crossed the Green March towards Liathaven.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Mentioned in passing: the Feni exiles passed through Southmoor under Imperial escort.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: not named; the page mentions the Necropolis quayside and the docks of Sanctuary Sands, where Jachin's Legacy's burning beasts caused small fires.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Already held, Bittershore counts among the four regions giving the Empire control of Ossium. Druj magic made the forests along its edges hostile.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Thule conquered the Bonewood and declared complete dominance there, while the Imperial armies deliberately avoided it.
r.Ossium/Echofell: The Imperial armies stormed the Amber Scorpion's Tower of the Scorpion and conquered the region, overcoming hidden rope-bridge ambushes and a final Druj counter-attack.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: The five Imperial armies marched east out of the Galath Fields. It remains one of the four regions the Empire holds.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Empire conquered the Webwood against Druj warbands and the spider-heralds of Arhallogen, though the hidden temple was never found.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: Mentioned in passing: not named; Redoubt as a whole suffers Naeve's Twisting Blight.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: The Lasambrian Jotun took Anduz in a three-hour siege and now control the whole region, including Old Anduz and the Longing Circle. Freeborn there must submit or be exiled, and Faraden are barred.
r.Segura/Anozeseri: Lasambrians made significant progress conquering Anozeseri and the Corazón took the Golden Terraces. Their envoys delivered their terms at Anozel.
r.Segura/Burnish: Corazón raiders struck Sunsong Ranch in eastern Burnish. Losing its Towers of Anduz would end the great work's benefit.
r.Segura/Iron Plains: Corazón raiders destroyed the produce of the Red Fields on the Iron Plains.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Zemress refugees here were raided, and Lasambrian Jotun now occupy the Sobral Stand forest, the site of an upcoming conjunction.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: The Zemress refugees settled in Yellow Chase suffered Corazón raids. Its Towers of Anduz are at risk if the orcs advance.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Jotun Shield of the Mountain left its position near Wreck on the East Floes to march south against the Imperial armies.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: About nine-tenths of Sealtoq was retaken, but Yrsa Jansdóttir still holds Atalaq. A conjunction will open on Atalaq Tasanko before its gates.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Mentioned in passing: named only as an objective in several generals' orders.

A force to be reckoned with.d: The Sumaah had reopened Zemeh and invited pilgrims to Timoj, but still held the Imperial Crown and rejected the Synod. Asavea's civil war continued, and Almodin Oktístis faced trial for idolatry. The Senate ended Jarm's favoured trader status, while the Lantir question pushed Jarm and the Commonwealth towards war. The Sarcophan Kruidenkenner offered to build herb warehouses. Faraden trade suffered from Lasambrian Jotun incursions and an iridescent gloaming blight. The Iron Confederacy, angry over liao smuggling and Imperial maps, later received a treaty sharing territorial knowledge and criminalising the liao trade. Tsark remained enigmatic. The summit agreed sanctions on Jarm, Asavea, Faraden, Thule and the Iron Confederacy.

n.Dawn: Dawnish citizens served as ambassadors to Asavea and the Iron Confederacy. The Kruidenkenner were interested in building a herb warehouse in Dawn, and Faraden merchants wanted access to Dawnish luxuries, though their hopes were fading.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Druj-held Zenith is named only as lying west of the Mountains of the Moon, where Tsark was discovered.
n.Grendel: Under the treaty ratified with the Iron Confederacy, the Empire agreed to share its knowledge of Grendel territories with the Suranni.
n.Highguard: The Sumaah Houses of Virtue declared they no longer recognised Bastion as the heart of the Way, and a Highborn, Accalon of Felix's Watch, served as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun's attack on Segura disrupted Faraden caravans: they refused to let western travellers trade in the land they had claimed, though they would not breach their treaty with Faraden.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants concluded that the success of Moonwater Hall was unlikely to be repeated elsewhere in the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: The Lasambrian attack on Segura disrupted Faraden trade, the Suranni accused the Empire of letting liao be smuggled through Feroz, and the Brass Coast's Gonzalo i Riqueza served as Ambassador to Faraden.
n.The League: League citizen Guillamo de Tassato was alleged to have stolen the Imperial Crown for the Sumaah. Jarmish magicians traded through the Tassato Mana Exchange, and engineer Menno van Ritsjhof left to visit the Commonwealth with the League Assembly's blessing.
n.The Marches: The Sarcophan Kruidenkenner expressed interest in building a herb-trading warehouse in the Marches, an opportunity open until the end of the Spring Equinox 383YE.
n.Thule: Thule was explicitly named among the slaving nations against which the Empire agreed to enact trade sanctions after the summit.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's Tarquinius Ankarien is named as the Imperial Ambassador to Axos.
n.Varushka: Sarcophan merchants were travelling in growing numbers through Varushka's forests and hills, and Faraden merchants wanted Varushkan timber and ore through an enclave in Volodmartz, though the Empire showed little interest.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark citizens served as ambassadors to Jarm and the Sarcophan Delves, Kallavesa proposed the motion ending Jarm's favoured trader status, and the Kruidenkenner considered building a warehouse in the nation.

t.Astolat: Faraden merchants hoped for a trading enclave in central Astolat to reach Dawnish luxuries, but admitted the Empire seemed to have little interest in the idea.
t.Bastion: The Sumaah Houses of Virtue formally declared that they no longer recognised the White City of Bastion as the heart of the Way, urging pilgrims to look to Timoj instead.
t.Bay of Catazar: Sarcophan merchants were common in the towns around the bay, and Imperial captains' earlier mapping of it led to Suranni accusations of espionage, later answered by a treaty sharing that knowledge.
t.Feroz: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz kept bringing profit from Asavean trade, while the Suranni insisted that liao was being smuggled into the Iron Confederacy through Feroz.
t.Karsk: The Kruidenkenner enclave at chill Ivarsgard had brought a marked rise in Sarcophan merchants travelling through the eastern territories and more herbs reaching the auction at Anvil.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Siroc is listed among the places where Sarcophan merchants and traders were a common sight.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the success of Moonwater Hall is cited as something Faraden merchants no longer expected to see repeated elsewhere in the Empire.
t.Mountains of the Moon: After the spy network into the mountains was completed and the nation of Tsark revealed, there were no further developments, and Tsark remained enigmatic.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Sanctuary Sands is listed among the places where Sarcophan merchants were a common sight.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the smaller neighbours known to practise slavery, with no sign of its representatives attending the summit.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named directly. Its only link to the page is Urizen's Tarquinius Ankarien, named as Ambassador to Axos.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is noted for the sea fortifications Menno van Ritsjhof designed for it and as a place where Sarcophan traders were common.
t.Segura: The Lasambrian Jotun's attack on Segura left them barring Faraden travellers from the land they had claimed, disrupting western trade with the Empire. The page warned this could worsen if they took more Brass Coast land.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is named only as lying west of the Mountains of the Moon, where Tsark was discovered.
t.Tassato: An enclave of Jarmish magicians continued to work through the Tassato Mana Exchange, importing Beloye zerno for sale to Imperial citizens with mana sites.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named directly; the Marches as a whole are among the nations where the Kruidenkenner considered building a herb warehouse.
t.Volodmartz: Faraden merchants wanted a trading enclave in Volodmartz to reach Varushkan timber and ore, but conceded the Empire seemed to have little interest.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is named only as lying west of the Mountains of the Moon, where Tsark was discovered.

r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: Sanctuary Sands is listed among the places along the Bay of Catazar where Sarcophan merchants were a common sight.

A hero's welcome.d: Crowds in Siroc, Necropolis, Sarvos and elsewhere greeted the returning fleets. Inspired by Eska Crowspeaker's mandate, the people housed the freed slaves wherever there was space. Nearly two hundred humans, mostly foreigners, were given the means to go home, as were a handful of Jotun, Thule, Druj and other foreign orcs. The great majority, orcs of the Broken Shore, hate the Grendel, are grateful to the Empire and wish to stay. The civil service suggested Skarsind, the Brass Coast or a League city as homes. The General Assembly upheld Skywise Tulva's mandate for Skarsind by a greater margin than Arno von Leche's competing mandate for the League. It also upheld Eska Crowspeaker's mandate to spread the Way to them.

n.Druj: A few freed Druj were among the rescued orcs and left for home almost at once, despite some concern about returning sworn enemies of the Empire.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost treasure and nearly two thousand slaves taken from Dubhtraig, and the freed orcs of the Broken Shore now burn with hatred for their former masters.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: crowds in Necropolis were among those welcoming the returning fleets.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skywise Tulva's winning mandate invites the freed orcs to settle in Skarsind, fight their former enslavers or support the legions, and in time become Imperial Orcs by adopting their ways.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a handful of the freed orcs were Jotun, who returned home quickly despite some unease.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the welcome of the Great Forest orcs into Therunin is cited as a precedent for settling newcomers.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsairs rescued many of the slaves, and settling them in the Brass Coast was proposed, but no Freeborn mandate was upheld.
n.The League: The League was proposed as a home for the more ambitious former house slaves, and Arno von Leche's mandate to settle them in League cities was upheld but lost to the Skarsind mandate on margin.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: stalled attempts to bring the thralls of the Mournwold to the Way are cited as a warning about converting the freed orcs.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a handful of the freed orcs were Thule, who sought to return home.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, though the fleets returning from the Broken Shore landed at Imperial ports.
t.Holberg: Holberg was suggested as a possible home for the freed orcs if the Senate funded 15 thrones of travel support, but the League mandate did not prevail.
t.Madruga: Crowds in Siroc welcomed the returning fleets and about a third of the freed slaves were already there, making it a ready option for settling them in the Brass Coast, though this was not chosen.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: attempts to bring the Mournwold's thralls to the Way have stalled, a cautionary example.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: crowds lined the docks of Necropolis to welcome the victorious fleets.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos welcomed the returning fleets and could have taken the freed orcs at no cost, with the College of the Liberated to help them, but the League mandate lost to the Skarsind mandate.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the settlement of the Zemress islanders in Segura is cited as a precedent for welcoming newcomers.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind will receive the freed orcs of the Broken Shore under Skywise Tulva's winning mandate, a long journey the Senate could ease with 20 thrones of support.
t.Tassato: Tassato was named as a League city where the freed orcs could have settled at no cost, but the League mandate did not prevail.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar was suggested as a possible home if the Senate funded 15 thrones of travel support, but the League mandate did not prevail.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the earlier welcome of the Great Forest orcs into Therunin is cited as a precedent.

A time of plenty.d: Backed by the Prosperity Assembly (152-0), Gilah consecrated the Kraken's Bane, drawing more pilgrims to Calvos Sound and prompting new paradors and plans to expand the dock. Gabriela's seminary would stand on a wharf, with a library and an etched mithril floor depicting Zemress' life. It would cost 15 wains each of weirwood, white granite and mithril plus 45 crowns. The Zemress islanders offered to build it and pay the crowns. The Sumaah Republic offered all the granite or the weirwood and copies of its records of Zemress, if the seminary stayed open to all followers of the Way. The offers lapse unless work begins by the Summer Solstice 383YE.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Gilah's statement of principle hoped the consecrated shrine would bolster those who follow Zemress' example in raiding the Grendel.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a newly consecrated shrine to their exemplar Zemress, with growing pilgrim trade and an Imperial commission for her seminary. The Zemress islanders pledged to build it and pay its 45 crowns themselves.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named on the page; the only link is a section heading, 'What the Morrow Holds'.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is recalled as the waters Zemress cleared of pirates from the deck of the Kraken's Bane, earning her the title Blade of the Isles.
t.Madruga: Madruga hosts the consecrated Kraken's Bane, and the Senate commissioned a seminary to Zemress there, drawing pilgrims from across the Empire and from Sumaah.

r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Calvos Sound, Zemress' birthplace, saw her ship consecrated and a rising flood of pilgrims, with new paradors opening and plans to expand the dry dock. The Senate commissioned a wharf-top seminary to be built beside the Bane.

Appraisal of Feni dispersion.d: The motion sought a civil service appraisal of what it would cost to deal with the Woods-that-Fell Feni, who were causing disruption in northern Hercynia, either by dispersing them or arresting them using the militia or private citizens. It was proposed by Hercynia and seconded by Hahnmark. Only one appraisal may be commissioned each season. The motion failed, so no appraisal was made and the Senate was given no costed option for removing the Feni by these means.

n.Navarr: Navarr's senator for Hercynia brought the motion to get a costed plan for handling the Feni in Navarr-held land, but its failure left the nation with no Senate-backed appraisal of the problem.

t.Hercynia: The disruption caused by the Woods-that-Fell Feni in northern Hercynia remained without a costed plan to disperse or arrest them, because the appraisal motion failed.

Assignment of Ossium.d: The motion, proposed by Karov and seconded by Volomartz, sought to assign the territory of Ossium to Varushka, and it passed in Winter 382YE. As a result Ossium became a Varushkan territory and went on to appoint a Senator, giving it representation in the Imperial Senate as part of Varushka.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named in the motion, though Ossium was recorded as theirs that season; its assignment to Varushka treats it as an Imperial territory.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained Ossium as one of its territories, and the territory appointed a Senator to sit for it.

t.Ossium: Ossium was formally assigned to Varushka by the Senate, became a Varushkan territory and appointed a Senator.

Between peace and hate.d: The Thule delivered about 150 human slaves freed from the Bonewood to Ivarsgard, postponed ransom talks and rejected the Imperial claim to Sungold Pass. The Great Forest orcs described the Mallum and offered scouts to map it. The Thralls in the Mournwold refused to cooperate with magistrates. Grendel pirates continued to penalise trading fleets. The Jotun were angered by undead and the destruction of the Meeting Place, while the Lasambrians demanded Segura and Feroz. Druj envoys offered Urizen a ceasefire bound by Sorin's oath. Afterwards the Conclave agreed to share a ritual with Otkodov, the Varushkan assembly sent Belakov to examine the slaves, and the Senate declined the mapping but resumed the Holt of the Oak.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a handful of the freed slaves at Ivarsgard have links to Dawn.
n.Druj: Druj envoys, backed by a herald of Sorin, offered the leaders of Urizen a ceasefire covering Morrow and adjacent territories, sealed by a sanguine oath. Meanwhile the Great Forest orcs revealed what they knew of the Mallum's lands, fortresses and slave labour.
n.Grendel: The Grendel armada stayed anchored off Sarvos, while independent pirates, some serving Siakha, raided Imperial shipping. Innevia, daughter of Salt Lord Moorvain, and fifty other prisoners were released after negotiations with General Talbot.
n.Highguard: Highguard trading fleets faced a one-rank production penalty from Grendel piracy. The Great Forest orcs offered their scouts to their Highguard and Navarr allies, and a few of the freed slaves have Highborn links.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Thralls prefer to deal directly with representatives of the Imperial Orcs and the Marchers, and Marchers noted the travelling Thralls were clearly not from Skarsind.
n.Jotun: The northern Jotun held all of Sermersuaq and were enraged by risen dead and the destruction of the Meeting Place, yet Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir sent a message to the Military Council. The Lasambrian Jotun demanded Segura and Feroz in exchange for a ceasefire.
n.Navarr: Around two hundred Great Forest orcs now walk the trods with Navarr stridings, and the Thule were bringing a dragon-made ritual text for the vate Merel. The Senate approved resuming work on the Holt of the Oak.
n.The Brass Coast: The Lasambrian Jotun claimed Segura and Feroz as ancestral lands and offered peace only if both were ceded or conquered, promising that Freeborn who stayed could join their nation. Brass Coast fleets also faced the Grendel trade penalty.
n.The League: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos suffered the Grendel piracy penalty as the armada stayed anchored off Sarvos. The senator for Sarvos had seconded the motion claiming Sungold Pass.
n.The Marches: Marchers struggled to adjust to the Thralls of the Mournwold as brawls broke out and the orcs refused to help magistrates, following Anna Pernn's statement of principle. A trio of Thralls clashed with Faraden in Hay.
n.Thule: The Thule held the Bonewood, freed its human slaves to Karsk, denied using forced cannibalism, delayed ransom talks and rejected the Imperial claim to Sungold Pass. Grand Warlock Fljajokull's visit led the Conclave to agree to share a ritual with Otkodov.
n.Urizen: The Druj insisted on presenting ceasefire terms only to Urizen's leaders, offering an oath enforced by Sorin. Urizen fleets also faced the Grendel trade penalty.
n.Varushka: Most of the 150 freed slaves at Ivarsgard were Varushkan or of Varushkan descent, and the national assembly sent Belakov the Wolf of Karsk to examine their true nature. Imperial and Thule forces were also in a standoff at Sungold Pass.
n.Wintermark: An emissary of the Queen of Kalsea approached Wintermark's armies near Sealtoq. The Jotun blamed Imperials for smashing the Meeting Place stone but saw a contradiction with Wintermark's honourable conduct, leaving a chance to restore trust.

t.Bay of Catazar: Independent Grendel pirates, including bloodthirsty Siakha worshippers with sharks and unnatural weather, stepped up raids on Imperial trading ships in the Bay.
t.Bregasland: Jotun scouting parties were reported in Bregasland's marshes, and some adventurous Thralls travelled there from the Mournwold.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest orcs offered support against the vallorn here, with details given elsewhere.
t.Feroz: The Lasambrian Jotun claimed Feroz as ancestral land and demanded it be ceded or conquered before they would make peace.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The Great Forest orcs described a huge slave-worked mine, rich weirwood groves and an immense fortress said to house a powerful buruk tepel master of poisons.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Thralls seemed oddly reluctant to travel south into Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Jotun scouting parties were reported tentatively exploring the marshes of Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the senator for Karov, Vuk the Wolfeater, had proposed the motion claiming Sungold Pass.
t.Karsk: Nearly 150 freed slaves were delivered to Ivarsgard, leaving the town unsure whether to welcome them, and Belakov the Wolf of Karsk was sent to examine them for interlopers.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: some Thralls travelled north into Mitwold after the harvest.
t.Morrow: Druj envoys and a draughir herald approached the Imperial position in Morrow under a flag of truce to propose a ceasefire.
t.Mournwold: The Thralls brought in their harvests and went to fairs, but brawls followed and they refused all cooperation with the magistrates, while doubts about their faith persisted.
t.Ossium: Thule warriors conquered and held the Bonewood and freed its human slaves, while the Great Forest orcs, never sent there by the Druj, sought to walk the trods into it.
t.Otkodov: Peace with the orcs of Otkodov held, though they pressed their claim to Sungold Pass. The Conclave declared it would share a ritual with them.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Great Forest orcs described watery plains and the port of Leen, which they believe is the Mallum's largest settlement and a place where the Grendel trade.
t.Sarangrave: The Great Forest orcs described the Sarangrave as fertile slave plantations with an ancient white-granite fortress and a malignant presence in the marsh.
t.Sarvos: The Grendel armada remained anchored off Sarvos, and its trading fleets faced the piracy penalty.
t.Segura: Three Lasambrian Jotun armies made inroads into Segura and demanded the whole territory, offering a Spring Equinox summit if the remaining regions were ceded.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun still held all of Sermersuaq after undead rose from its battlefields, and Wintermark's armies camped there received the Queen of Kalsea's emissary.
t.Skarsind: Thule work on Crow's Keep continued apace, with completion expected before Summer 383YE, and Jotun raiders were sighted at Pakaanan's Pass.
t.Tassato: Tassato's trading fleets suffered the Grendel piracy penalty, and some Thralls travelled there from the Mournwold.
t.The Barrens: The Great Forest orcs described the Barrens as the Druj's coveted hub for moving armies. The Imperial spy network there had been destroyed but could be rebuilt.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest orcs remained in Therunin, dealing with Senator Cybi Farkas, and the Senate approved resuming work on the Holt of the Oak there.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: some Thralls travelled north into Upwold after the harvest.
t.Volodmartz: Imperial and Thule forces watched each other over Sungold Pass, which Otkodov refused to concede, and the Minister of Historical Research commissioned further investigation of the mine.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: A Thule warband emerged from the hills of Krevsaty to deliver the freed slaves to Ivarsgard.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Mentioned in passing: the Thralls seemed reluctant to cross the Greensward south into Kahraman.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Thule warriors conquered and held the Bonewood and freed all of its roughly 150 human slaves, while the fate of its far more numerous orc slaves remained unknown.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Mentioned in passing: in the opening tale, a dragon ordered a merchant to send word to Nithoggir after surveying the mine.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Mentioned in passing: new Thule towers at Crow's Keep overlook the passes into Urdur.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: The Queen of Kalsea's emissary approached the Wintermark armies camped south of the ancient town of Sealtoq.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: Thule fortifications at Crow's Keep overlook the passes into the Silver Peaks.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Small groups of Jotun raiders were sighted as far east as Pakaanan's Pass.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Senate approved resuming work on the Holt of the Oak fortification in the Lower Tarn Valley.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: Sungold Pass, claimed by the Senate as part of Opascari, remained in an Imperial–Thule standoff, with a historical research investigation of the ruins commissioned.

Bills or bows.d: Inspired by popular love for their generals and Friar John's mandate, all Marcher armies may now fight shoulder to shoulder, holding the line with bill blocks and archers. For one year, the Senate could commission the Drakes' enlargement for 125 wains of mithril or weirwood, with wealthy yeomen covering the money. A motion to do so was brought, but the page does not record its outcome. The Bounders and the Strong Reeds could each change quality for 25 wains. Abbot Thomas Arch supplied 44 wains of mithril and 6 of weirwood, so the Bounders became watchful and the Strong Reeds secretive. The Tusks' general appointment will move to the Spring Equinox from 384YE.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a pair of Jotun orcs are seen meeting a poacher at the edge of the Mourn in the opening story, and the Strong Reeds are noted for their history of resisting Jotun aggression.
n.The Marches: Every Marcher army can now fight shoulder to shoulder. The Bounders became watchful and the Strong Reeds secretive, the Drakes were offered an enlargement, and the Tusks' general appointment is being moved to the Spring Equinox.

t.Bregasland: The Strong Reeds, long tied to Bregasland's people, turned back to old fen-honed stratagems and became a secretive army able to lay low in marsh, forest and mountain regions.
t.Mitwold: The Drakes, many of whose soldiers come from Mitwold, were offered the chance to be enlarged and armed with bills or bows, funded by wealthy Marcher yeomen and 125 wains of mithril or weirwood.
t.Mournwold: The Mandate came from Friar John of the Mourn, and recruits from the Mournwold have swelled the Drakes' ranks. Its barren mountains are named as the kind of terrain where the newly secretive Strong Reeds can lay low.
t.Upwold: The Bounders, built around Upwold beaters and landskeepers, gave up their slaughtering tactics to become a watchful army able to harry the flanks or watch the passes.

r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story, a poacher from Alderly Edge is seen secretly meeting Jotun at the edge of the Mourn.

Construct Emilio's Herbarium.d: Palerictus Krunk announced that the Imperial Orcs would use their Imperial Wayleave to build a sinecure in Foracci, Sarvos. It was to be called Emilio's Herbarium, and the announcement linked it to the Anvil hospital. When complete it will create the Imperial title of Keeper of Emilio's Herbarium, a tenure position appointed by the Loyalty assembly. The commission uses standard costs, but its size was not specified. After the Winter Solstice 382YE, Giacomo Corvinoscuro supplied 12 weirwood and 24 crowns towards it. The page does not record the sinecure as finished.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs spent their Wayleave on this commission, announced by Palerictus Krunk, to establish a weirwood-herb sinecure tied to the Anvil hospital.
n.The League: The sinecure is being raised in the League territory of Sarvos, under an Imperial Wayleave held by another nation.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos is to host Emilio's Herbarium, a new sinecure whose keeper will be appointed by the Loyalty assembly. Weirwood and crowns were delivered towards it after the Winter Solstice.

r.Sarvos/Foracci: Foracci is the chosen site for Emilio's Herbarium, which received its first materials after the Winter Solstice 382YE.

Construct Freya's Garden.d: The motion, raised under Tyr Brennan's Imperial Wayleave, commissioned a Great Work in the Wintermark territory of Hahnmark at standard cost, to be named Freya's Garden. After the Winter Solstice 382YE, Tyr Brenna provided 50 wains of weirwood and 100 crowns towards its construction. The recorded outcome is that the work yields a bounty of 84 herbs, divided between the owners of herb gardens in Hahnmark. Its stated purpose is to supply herbs that heal the Empire.

n.Wintermark: A Wintermark-held territory gains a Great Work dedicated to healing herbs, commissioned under a Wintermark wayleave by Tyr Brennan, which enriches the nation's herb garden owners in Hahnmark.

t.Hahnmark: Freya's Garden is built in Hahnmark, and its bounty of 84 herbs is shared among the territory's herb garden owners.

Construct Georgies' Home for Goodest Dog.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Morrow, the motion commissioned a business sinecure in Holberg at standard cost, though the size of the commission was not specified. It passed, and the title is to be assigned each year by the League's Senators. After the Winter Solstice 382YE, Victor van Holberg provided 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns towards its construction. When complete, the sinecure will create a new Imperial title, the Custodian of the Kennels.

n.The League: The League's Senators will choose the holder of the Custodian of the Kennels each year, and Victor van Holberg supplied the first white granite and crowns for the work.

t.Holberg: Holberg is to host Georgies Home for Goodest Dogs, a new business sinecure whose construction is under way with materials provided by Victor van Holberg.

Construct Kalpaheim Tradehall.d: Proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion commissioned a trade hall in Kalpaheim in line with a recent proposal. The commission used non-standard costs of 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, with three months needed to complete it. Hengest Dunn provided the weirwood and the crowns after the Spring Equinox 383YE. The completed hall is a ministry that creates a new title, the Kalpaheim Tradeholder, and it is described as a very productive tradehall tied into the Northern Trade Network.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's artisans and traders, who requested the hall, gained a productive ministry linked to the Northern Trade Network, along with the new title of Kalpaheim Tradeholder.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's senator proposed the motion, and the Kalpaheim Tradehall was to be built within the territory as a ministry connected to the Northern Trade Network.

Construct Kobarid Jewelers.d: Proposed by Temeschwar and seconded by Madruga, the motion sought to build a ministry in Miaren from which the Kobarid family of Jarm would sell glazamy neba to Imperial customers. The opportunity arose from an offer by the Jarmish Magician-Prince Matvei Kobarid and was raised again after an earlier motion to build the jewellers was abrogated. The project would have cost 8 White Granite, 4 Mithril and 24 Crowns, to be self-funded, and would have created the title of Star Jeweler, appointed by Imperial Bourse auction. The motion failed.

n.Navarr: Navarr would have hosted a Jarmish-run jewellery exchange and the new Star Jeweler title on its land, but the motion failed and nothing was built.

t.Miaren: Miaren was the proposed site of the fortified Jarmish Jewellery Exchange, but the failed motion meant no construction took place there.

Construct Mithril Block.d: The motion commissioned the Block in Cinion as laid out in earlier proposals, and it passed with no throne cost. Construction was set at the non-standard cost of 40 wains of mithril and 80 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 382YE, Edmundo of Damakhan's Forge provided 22 wains of mithril, and Maximilian provided 18 wains of mithril and 10 thrones. Once complete, the Block would remove the penalties suffered by mana sites, congregations, herb gardens, mines and forests owned by those living in Spiral. Its protection would also let people live in Spiral despite the curse of the Black Plateau, slightly speeding the territory's recovery and its contributions to Imperial coffers.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page, though it held part of Spiral, the territory the Block is meant to protect.
n.Urizen: The Senator for Spiral, a territory Urizen held at least in part, proposed the Block. Once complete, it promised to lift the curse-related penalties on Spiral residents' mana sites, congregations, herb gardens, mines and forests.

t.Spiral: The Block would shield Spiral's spires from the curse of the Black Plateau. It would make the territory feasibly habitable again, remove production penalties on its residents' resources and slightly increase its rate of recovery.

r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion was chosen as the site of the Block, a mithril ward with three months of construction to follow the commission.

Construct Naval Academy of Blood and Bra.d: Proposed by Feroz, the motion sought to construct the Naval Academy of Blood and Brass in the city of Siroc to the designs of Frederick di Sarvos, as a school of shipbuilding and international trade. The Great Work was to be funded half by Lorenzo La Volpe von Temeschwar as a Butcher's Benevolence and half by the New Promise Cartel of the Brass Coast, offered as a gift to the Empire celebrating the victory over the Grendel of Dubhtraig. The seconder is unrecorded. The motion failed, so the academy was not commissioned.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the motion framed the academy as a celebration of the Empire's victory over the Grendel of Dubhtraig.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's New Promise Cartel offered to fund half of a shipbuilding and trade academy in Siroc, but the motion failed and the Brass Coast did not gain the school.

t.Madruga: Siroc in Madruga would have hosted the Naval Academy of Blood and Brass had the motion passed, but it failed and nothing was built there.

Construct Quartermaster's ministry.d: Proposed by Skarsind and seconded by Karov, the motion amended the title of Quartermaster General to include a ministry in Casinea through which mana could be purchased. The ministry was to use standard costs, though the size of the commission was not specified. The motion passed. After the Summer Solstice 383YE, Rurik provided 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns towards its construction. Once complete, the ministry is to be assigned to the Quartermaster General.

n.Highguard: Highguard gains a mana ministry on its soil in Casinea, although control of it rests with the Quartermaster General rather than with any Highborn office.

t.Casinea: Casinea is the site chosen for the new ministry, where the Quartermaster General will be able to purchase mana once construction is complete.

Construct Sarcombe Register II.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Skarsind, the motion commissioned the Sarcombe Register as a folly in the newly established market town of Sarcombe. It created the position of Custodian of the Registry, appointed for life by the Marcher senators and revocable by the Marcher Assembly. The commission used non-standard costs of 6 wains of white granite and 12 crowns of labour, with three months to complete. Orrick of House Bolholt provided the granite and crowns after the Spring Equinox 383YE. Once built, the Register helped friars find families willing to take in orphans.

n.The Marches: Marcher senators gained the power to appoint a Custodian of the Registry for life, subject to revocation by the Marcher Assembly, and Orrick of House Bolholt funded the construction.

t.Mournwold: Sarcombe in the Mournwold became home to the Register, where friars worked to place the territory's orphans with willing families.

Construct Zemress seminary.d: Proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by Kahraman, the motion commissioned a seminary celebrating the life of the exemplar Zemress, with the help of Prince Jonah von Holberg of the Printer's Guild. It used non-standard costs of 15 wains each of weirwood, white granite and mithril, taking three months to build. Adan i DelToro i Riqueza supplied the weirwood and all 15 wains of mithril across two seasons, the Zemress islanders contributed 45 crowns, and the Sumaah Republic provided the white granite. Although the motion would have lapsed at the Winter Solstice 383YE if unfinished, the seminary was completed after the Summer Solstice 383YE.

n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast senators and citizens drove the project: Madruga's senator proposed it, Adan i DelToro i Riqueza supplied most of the materials, and a new seminary to the exemplar Zemress now stands in their lands.

t.Madruga: Madruga gained the Seminary of Zemress, completed after the Summer Solstice 383YE, which was built to celebrate the exemplar and welcome pilgrims from around the world.

Construct repairs to Heliopticon.d: Proposed by the Senator for Redoubt and seconded by Astolat, the motion passed at 27 Thrones and 2 Crowns. The work required 12 wains of mithril and 24 Crowns and would take three months. It also adds costs to each Urizen territory and the usual upkeep of a college of magic, currently 25 Thrones. After the Winter Solstice, Andronikos provided 2 wains of mithril and the 24 Crowns, and Edmundo of Damakhan's Forge provided the other 10 wains. The Doyen of the Spires is chosen by a majority of Urizen's magicians and holds the title until they codify one arcane projection. The Synod can revoke it. Research speed depends on how many Urizen territories are connected to the network.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but the commission covers the central heliopticon tower in Spiral, which Grendel held at the time.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Heliopticon is to be rebuilt, giving its magicians the role of a college of magic and the right to choose a Doyen of the Spires. The project also adds costs to each Urizen territory.

t.Morrow: Morrow is home to one of the central heliopticon towers that the commission was raised to repair.
t.Spiral: The commission includes repairing the central heliopticon tower in Spiral, although the territory was in Grendel hands at the time.

Construct the Hearth of Virtue.d: Raised in Winter 382YE as an Imperial wayleave by Nikolovich Drakov, the commission was for a seminary school called the Hearth of Virtue in Perumaki, Miekarova, at standard sinecure costs. Drakov supplied 20 wains of granite and 8 thrones after the Winter Solstice 382YE, and 3 thrones were returned to him after the Summer Solstice 383YE. The completed sinecure creates a new Imperial title, the Tender of the Hearth. The title has tenure and is appointed by the Varushkan National Assembly. The in-character text had named that assembly as the body able to revoke the appointment.

n.Varushka: Varushka gains a seminary meant to prove its devotion to the Way, and the Varushkan National Assembly appoints its tenured title holder, the Tender of the Hearth.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova becomes home to a new sinecure, the Hearth of Virtue seminary, which brings with it the Imperial title of Tender of the Hearth.

r.Miekarova/Perumaki: The Hearth of Virtue seminary is built in Perumaki, using granite and thrones supplied by Nikolovich Drakov.

Crafted from torment.d: Ossium had almost no native Imperial citizens, so it could go to any of the ten nations. The civil service stressed that contiguity barely mattered thanks to the egregores. Known inhabitants were the morose orc Sand Fishers, the Varushkan-descended Ketsov humans and Druj of the Bone Serpent Clan, though the Empire had no map. Each nation's case was weighed: the League, Varushka, the Marches and the Brass Coast offered the best tax prospects, Dawn the most military support. Relinquishment was possible but risky. The Senate assigned Ossium to Varushka, which elected its first senator, and recognised the Sand Fishers as foreigners. The Ketsov's status remained uncertain.

n.Dawn: Dawn's case rested on the magical Golden Bridge to Lacre, Barrens refugees keen to settle and the Semmerlak's Summer links. Ossium would have given Dawn the most military support but little taxation, and the Senate did not choose it.
n.Druj: Ossium was conquered from the Druj, and the Bone Serpent Clan still had a significant presence there. Those unable to join the new nation might flee east to their kin or remain as a dangerous barbarian population.
n.Highguard: Highguard was argued to offer the fastest conversion of Ossium's people to the Way and secluded land for monastic chapters, though the new pilgrimage meant it could ill afford to lose more citizens.
n.Imperial Orcs: The civil service warned that the cowed Sand Fishers were as unlike the Imperial Orcs as possible. Ossium's warmer lands might still have attracted orc settlers, but the nation would have yielded little tax and still faced its population problems.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun thralls in the Mournwold were cited as a precedent for foreigners living in the Empire, and the Jotun conquest of Sermersuaq was noted as having displaced people.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were presented as the best woodsfolk to face the dark northern forests, which adjoin Sküld's vallorn. They were also seen as best able to help displaced inhabitants resettle peacefully.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn case rested on draining marshes for docks and perhaps a shipyard on the Semmerlak, and on lifting the despairing Sand Fishers' spirits. It offered good long-term taxation but needed costly development.
n.The League: The League's case rested on the towns of Ketsov and Lomaa, the trade-minded Ketsov and the territory's contiguity with Holberg. It promised the largest boost to the treasury but at great development cost.
n.The Marches: The Marches were noted for Ossium's likeness to Bregasland, Mournwold experience of cooperating with orc neighbours and Marcher skill at farming barren land. The territory could have supported an extra army relatively quickly.
n.Thule: The Thule border Ossium and seem to have a particular interest in its dark northern forests. Their prosperity as foreigners in the Silver Peaks was cited as an example, and how each nation would fare as their neighbour was weighed.
n.Urizen: Urizen was seen as best placed to exploit Ossium's powerful magical sites and to engage the literate Ketsov. It would gain the least economically or militarily, and linking the territory to the Heliopticon would be hard.
n.Varushka: Varushka received Ossium, adding a new territory with its own senator. The case for it rested on the Ketsov's Varushkan origins, adjacency to Varushkan lands, a great mithril mine already worked by Moresvah's miners and experience with dark powers and the Thule.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's case rested on Kallavesi experience of wetlands, potential settlers displaced from Sermersuaq and Skarsind, and heroes eager to face the dark forests. The poor relations between the Thule and the Mark were weighed as both a risk and a possible advantage.

t.Bregasland: Ossium was judged surprisingly similar to Bregasland, and some of its citizens might have been keen to settle there had the Marches received the territory.
t.Holberg: Holberg was cited as a past contested assignment and lies across the river from Ossium. Its crowded citizens might have moved to Lomaa or Ketsov had the League won the territory.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren was cited as a Navarr territory whose vallorn has long been cleared, now a settled forest haven.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: some Bregaslanders would welcome Ossium's distance from the nosy folk of Upwold and Mitwold.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold's Marchers were noted as the only Imperial humans with good experience of living alongside orcs, and its Jotun thralls served as a precedent. It was suggested the Sand Fishers might even join the Mournwold Thralls.
t.Ossium: Ossium was assigned to Varushka and elected its first Imperial senator, while the Sand Fishers living there were recognised as foreigners under Imperial law. The status of the Ketsov and other former Druj subjects remained unsettled.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was compared to Reikos before the Highborn civilised it in the Empire's early years.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: people displaced when the Jotun conquered Sermersuaq were suggested as possible Wintermark settlers for Ossium.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind was cited as proof that a territory can change nation, and those who left it might have settled Ossium under Wintermark.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's joining the League was cited to show that Varushkan heritage need not bar League citizenship.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: some Bregaslanders would welcome Ossium's distance from the nosy folk of Upwold and Mitwold.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: the Thule prospering in the Silver Peaks was cited as evidence that foreigners can thrive within the Empire.

Draw strength from vulnerability.d: The Autumn 382YE mandate, upheld 164–0, named Ser Isidore Ossienne and Lord Colwyn de Rondell. Its preaching spread the view that love, like glory, takes many paths and that sex is not fundamental to it, changing Dawnish attitudes to love and marriage. Weavers of Spiral Castle made a Troubadour's Ring for the Champion of Love, and weavers of Laroc a Circlet of Command for the Champion of Glory. The egregore suggested bestowing them at the Grand Tourney. Troubadours proposed assembly statements of Love or Glory, to be spread by the Civil Service. Lady Zaha Arien designed the Arbor of the Twin Roses in Auvanne, which awaits a Senate commission or wayleave.

n.Dawn: Dawn's people embraced a broader, more varied understanding of True Love, reshaping national attitudes to love and marriage. Its troubadours gained new laurels for their Champions of Love and Glory, a way to honour inspiring figures through assembly statements, and plans for a pilgrimage monument with a new national title.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but the weavers of Spiral Castle, in Grendel-held Spiral, created the Troubadour's Ring for Dawn's Champion of Love.

t.Astolat: The Arbor of the Twin Roses is proposed for Auvanne, within sight of Endric's Hill, to honour the troubadour Elayne Silverlark. It would need a Senate commission or a wayleave to be built.
t.Semmerholm: The weavers of Laroc crafted the Circlet of Command for Dawn's Champion of Glory. The page also notes the Rose Towers built in Lacuve to celebrate Dawn's victories in Semmerholm and Weirwater.
t.Spiral: The weavers of Spiral Castle created the Troubadour's Ring, a garland for Dawn's Champion of Love that now rests with the egregore.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's victories in Weirwater are among those celebrated by the Rose Towers in Lacuve.

r.Semmerholm/Ferrond: The weavers of Laroc crafted the Circlet of Command, to be hallowed by Dawn's troubadours and bestowed on the Champion of Glory.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Mentioned in passing: the architect Lord Caradoc, Lady Zaha Arien's father, recently completed the Rose Towers in Lacuve to celebrate Dawn's victories.

Fight or flight.d: After conquering Zenith, five Druj armies attacked Morrow. The appraisal found that refugees could only leave safely under escort, either by an Imperial army making a heroic stand or by military units coordinated by the civil service. A combined fighting strength of 5000 could save at most 80% of the people. Redoubt was the preferred destination, then Bastion or Necropolis, while Therunin was risky. Evacuation would cut Morrow's taxes, move costs and some revenue to the receiving territory, and delay recovery if Morrow were retaken. Separately, Portia the Elder backed a plan to restore the Heliopticon (12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns) and create the Doyen of the Spires, chosen by Urizen magicians, to lead research across the spires.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the civil service apprentice Anton reminds himself he is no longer in Dawn and stops himself bowing.
n.Druj: Having taken Zenith and destroyed the Halls of Knowledge, five Druj armies were pressing their attack on Morrow, threatening to slaughter or enslave any Urizeni who fled without protection.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Spiral, which it held, contains one of the central Heliopticon towers the Senate commissioned to be repaired.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Bastion was named as the fallback refuge for Morrow's evacuees via the Couros bridge, with possible later dispersal to Necropolis. Reikos was ruled out as a destination.
n.Navarr: Navarr-held Therunin was judged a possible but dangerous refuge, as vallorn-infested regions could leave fleeing Urizeni trapped if the Druj pursued them.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the immortals of Otkodov are listed among the few magicians who could rival Urizen's mastery of magic.
n.Urizen: Urizen faced the possible evacuation and long-term depopulation of Morrow. It also gained the prospect of restoring its pride by linking its spires through a repaired Heliopticon under a Doyen of the Spires, elected by its magicians.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the civil servant Mila is Varushkan, and the Wise Ones of Varushka are imagined arguing that their nation should host any new college of magic.

t.Bastion: Bastion was the second-choice refuge for Morrow's people, reached over the bridge across the Couros. It would gain half of any tax revenue lost from Morrow, along with the matching support costs.
t.Morrow: Under Druj attack, Morrow could see up to 80% of its population evacuated, with matching losses of taxation. Its central Heliopticon tower was commissioned for repair, though heavy evacuation would stop it contributing to Urizen's magical research.
t.Necropolis: Refugees could not reach Necropolis directly across the Couros, but could disperse there from Bastion in a later season.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the sinister immortals of Otkodov are cited as rivals to Urizen's magical mastery.
t.Redoubt: The civil service recommended Redoubt as the best destination for Morrow's evacuees, along a good road towards Cargo. Redoubt would take on half of any lost revenue and the costs of supporting the refugees.
t.Reikos: Reikos was ruled out as a refuge because its roads and trods could not carry so many people to safety.
t.Spiral: Spiral's central Heliopticon tower was commissioned for repair as part of the plan to link Urizen's spires into a single research network.
t.Therunin: Therunin was considered a possible but hazardous destination for Morrow's refugees, since the vallorn could trap them if the Druj followed.
t.Zenith: Already conquered by the Druj, Zenith was where those who stayed suffered a terrible fate. Reclaiming it and restoring its Heliopticon would raise Urizen's research speed to 20 magnitude per season.

r.Therunin/Greenheart: The vallorn in Greenheart was one reason refugees sent to neighbouring Peakedge Song risked being trapped.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Peakedge Song was the region of Therunin to which Morrow's people could in theory be evacuated, though they risked being cornered there by pursuing Druj.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: The vallorn in Sweetglades hemmed in Peakedge Song, making it a dangerous refuge for fleeing Urizeni.

Focused and methodical.d: Frederick refused Viviane de Coeurdefer's request to design ten national colleges and to tour the Empire teaching. Instead he toured existing centres of learning and proposed four projects. One was expanding Holberg University with a Faculty of Architecture that would add an extra commission. Another was rebuilding Diora University in Sarvos with a College of Autumn Magic. A third was restoring the Lepidean Library in Highguard with a liao-producing Garden of Atun. The last was founding a School of Shipbuilding in Siroc. At the Winter Solstice no project was commissioned. Frederick paused all work pending an Inquisition called by Ranae de Rondell. The Lepidean Library was later commissioned in Winter 383YE. After Frederick left for the Commonwealth in 385YE, the opportunity closed.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Cardinal of Ambition, Viviane de Coeurdefer, prompted the opportunity with her Statement of Endeavour. Frederick rejected her specific requests for ten national colleges and a teaching tour, though her challenge inspired his alternative proposals.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj destruction of the Halls of Knowledge is cited as a reason to found a centralised college of magic at Diora.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of Sarvos is blamed for Diora University's troubles, and the Siroc school's site under the Salt Guard would make it harder for the Grendel to burn down.
n.Highguard: Highguard was offered the restoration of the Lepidean Library, which Nicovar had burned. The Heirs of Lepidus pledged to cover its labour and first upkeep if its Librarian became a Highborn national appointment. The library was eventually commissioned in Winter 383YE.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Frederick dismissed the idea of a university in a tiny Hercynian steading as a pointless folly.
n.The League: Three of the four proposals centred on League figures and cities: Frederick himself, the expansion of Holberg University and the renovation of Diora University in Sarvos. The Diora Chair of Dramaturgy was also floated as a possible League national title.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Frederick visited far Kalpaheim during his tour of the Empire's centres of learning.

t.Bastion: The White City in Bastion was proposed as the site of a restored Lepidean University and Library, enclosing the park that stands on the ruins Nicovar left. The library would include the Garden of Atun, producing an extra dose of true liao each season.
t.Bay of Catazar: Under the proposal, a Siroc School of Shipbuilding would let navies built there, and later any Imperial navy built on the Bay, gain a unique quality. It would also spark a wave of naval enthusiasm across the Bay.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Frederick used a tiny Hercynian steading as his example of where a university would be nothing but a giant folly.
t.Holberg: Holberg University, home of Frederick's own faculty, was offered four new faculties and a five-storey Faculty of Architecture tower. The expansion would also permanently upgrade the Wunderkind and Leger Domain.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim was among the places Frederick visited on his tour of centres of learning.
t.Sarvos: Diora University in Sarvos was proposed for a sweeping rebuild with mithril-mirrored towers and an international College of Autumn Magic and Dramaturgy. The Siroc school could also revive the Sarvos Arsenal and Dockyard opportunity.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato's decorative woodwork is one of the influences in Frederick's sketches for the Faculty of Architecture tower.

r.Bastion/Woodbury: Under the Lepidean Library proposal, the Heirs of Lepidus would move their books to the new library and eventually abandon their modest chapter house in Woodbury.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Under the Holberg proposal, the new arts campus would be built within Holmauer Park, and Katarzyna Von Carstein would be asked to lead that section of the work.

Fortify Lower Tarn Valley II.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Miekarova, the motion took up an offer from the Great Forest orcs. It called for 80 wains of weirwood, 20 thrones and a year's work, did not count against the Empire's limited commissions, and carried no upkeep while the orcs held the garrison. Work restarted at Winter 383YE. Contributions came from Cybi Farkas, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar, Vauraus Korppitkotka and the orcs themselves. Constitutionally, the motion amounted to ceding the fortification, though not the region, to the orcs. If the treaty broke and the orcs took the region, the fort could support them against Imperial forces.

n.Navarr: Navarr's senator for Therunin proposed the motion, accepting orc-built and orc-held defences in a Navarri territory in return for a fortification the Empire need not maintain.

t.Therunin: Therunin was to gain a rank one weirwood fortification garrisoned by the Great Forest orcs. This would strengthen the territory while the treaty held, but the fort could aid the orcs against the Empire if it failed.

r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Lower Tarn Valley was the site of the Holt of the Oak, to be built of weirwood and occupied by the Great Forest orcs. Construction restarted at Winter 383YE.

Handle with care.d: Hakima Razzia i Guerra offered a lead on the Ring of Atun sought by the Freeborn assembly, and the Highborn Heirs of Lepidus urged archivists to investigate. Khanum Hanima, a Faraden merchant, braved Jotun-dominated Reinos with mithril, coin and precious metals to buy gloaming. Navarr broker Gwyn Redpine planned to recruit young apprentices at the Academy. Hudeca Goodeye, a self-proclaimed maggot, brought modest loot from the Dubhtraig raid to sell. Ogpog, servant of the Azoth, announced a Night Market in the Hall of the Worlds, warning its goods might profoundly transfigure buyers. A cursed-seeming carved wooden map fragment from Varushka was added to the auction.

n.Grendel: Carpets, jewellery, weapons and furniture plundered from Dubhtraig during the successful Imperial raid, which freed slaves and burned Salt Lord Suriad's shipyard and palace, were being sold at Anvil.
n.Highguard: The Heirs of Lepidus hoped the ring might be Atun's original, lost after Permion's death, or another historic Highborn ring, and urged Highborn archivists to investigate; Terah of Highguard, the Gloaming Sentinel, was sought by the Faraden buyer.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden merchant had to cross Jotun-dominated Reinos, and Lasambrian-Jotun forces now held the eastern end of the gloaming trade route after conquering Anduzjasse.
n.Navarr: Therunin broker Gwyn Redpine came to recruit Academy apprentices aged 14 to 17, and Navarr merchants were invited to sell their gloaming stocks to Khanum Hanima.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly's call for the Ring of Atun drew a lead from hakima Razzia i Guerra, due to meet Sagua i Ezmara at the Forge, while the Freeborn Gloaming Road was shown to fall short of Faraden demand.
n.Urizen: Urizen merchants were invited to sell gloaming to the Faraden buyer, and the sought ring might be one of those Highborn artificers crafted as gifts to the Urizen.
n.Varushka: Varushkan merchants were sought as gloaming sellers, and a strange carved wooden map fragment brought out of Varushka by a terrified trader went to the public auction.
n.Wintermark: Hudeca Goodeye, a Wintermark raider more interested in loot than freeing slaves, planned to sell Dubhtraig treasures to newcomers at the Wintermark camp.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named; it is linked only through the raid on Dubhtraig whose plunder came to Anvil.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren's brokers are described as wealthier than those of Therunin.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden merchant's three mithril wagons crossed Jotun-dominated Reinos intact to reach the Empire.
t.Segura: Lasambrian-Jotun conquest of part of Segura left invaders controlling the eastern end of the gloaming trade route.
t.Therunin: Therunin's wealth in lumber, herbs, iridescent butterflies and more esoteric sources was described, and its broker Gwyn Redpine set out to recruit apprentices at Anvil.

r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Anduzjasse's conquest by invading Lasambrian-Jotun forces put the eastern end of the gloaming trade route under their control.

Lethal and elusive.d: The Liathaven vallorn was sliding into slumber under the thirty-year winter of Wither the Seed. Westwood could be cleared if Imperial armies, attacking from the West Ranging beachhead, claimed the entire region before the Summer Solstice 383YE, though miasma would double casualties. Surut offered further boons for a Navarr assault if granted amity again, in exchange for devouring the forest of Birchland, Tower March or Alderly. Liathaven's trods had been severed by unknown magic. The southern Feni and the Alderly survivors entered Liaven's Glen, where a Senate treaty allows them to live. The northern band raided Hercynia, targeting mana sites. The Senate declined to act, so the raids will hit Hercynia's production.
