n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks are named as one of the armies that fought the vallorn's expansion in Liathaven in Spring 382YE.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Empire had secured West Ranging from the Jotun, and Liaven's Glen, where the Feni have gone, is still technically in Jotun hands.
n.Navarr: The northern Feni became a Navarr problem, raiding Hercynia's steadings, trade routes and mana sites, while Surut offered fresh boons to aid a Navarr assault on Liathaven if he was granted amity and paid in advance.
n.The Marches: The southern Feni finally left the Mournwold after months of disruption, but Surut sought to devour one of three Marcher forests, Birchland, Tower March or Alderly, as the price of further aid.
n.Wintermark: The northern Feni band, swelled by local Feni, left Hahnmark for Hercynia after raids on Wintermark's halls and a failed peace attempt by the Suaq grimnir Kaukana Broken Wing.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande is described as stirring, in contrast with Liathaven, and its delaying techniques are cited as a comparison.
t.Hahnmark: The northern Feni of the Woods-that-Fell left Hahnmark for Hercynia, taking with them Feni who had dwelt in Hahnmark's gulleys and woodlands.
t.Hercynia: Feni raiders roamed southern Hercynia, and with the Senate declining to act, every farm and business faces a 36 ring production penalty and every mana site will yield one less crystal mana.
t.Liathaven: The vallorn was weakened and slumbering under a thirty-year winter, offering a brief chance to clear Westwood, while the territory's trods were severed and Feni bands settled in its east under a Senate treaty.
t.Mournwold: The southern branch of the Woods-that-Fell left the Mournwold for Liathaven, ending their disruption there.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim is named as one end of the Old Ranging trade route menaced by Feni bandits.
t.Upwold: Two Upwold forests, Birchland and Tower March, were among those Surut proposed to burn as payment for aiding the Navarr if amity was granted.

r.Hahnmark/Southridge: The northern Feni lingered in southern Southridge and gathered more Feni before moving on into Hercynia.
r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: The Feni crossed into Old Ranging and spread out, raiding unprepared steadings and the merchants on its important trade route.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: Minor Feni raids reached as far east as Summersend, though the bands showed no sign of moving into it in force.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: Liath's Heart is the vallorn's core and would be its only holding if Westwood were cleared, and a powerful Spring regio there or in Westwood is needed to restore the trods.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: The southern Feni and the survivors from Alderly passed into Liaven's Glen, beyond the ken of the Navarr.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: West Ranging served as the Empire's vital beachhead for any campaign against the vallorn, and is cited as already bearing the Burnt quality from Surut's fire.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Westwood could be wholly cleared of the vallorn if Imperial armies claimed the entire region before the Summer Solstice 383YE, at the cost of doubled casualties from the miasma.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Survivors of the Imperial attack on the Feni camp in Alderly followed the southern band into Liathaven, and Alderly's forest was one of three Surut offered to devour.
r.Upwold/Birchland: Birchland's forest was one Surut proposed to consume with magical fire, leaving it Burnt, as payment for further aid to the Navarr.
r.Upwold/Tower March: Tower March's forest was one Surut proposed to consume with magical fire, leaving it Burnt, as payment for further aid to the Navarr.

Moving mountains is no easy task.d: Highborn benefactors proposed the Cinderpath Exchange so that Highborn white granite could be sold at a virtuous price rather than auctioned at Anvil. The Senate rejected it twice, partly on misleading Civil Service information, but the Prosperity Assembly and Bartimaeus declared it virtuous. Similar grievances about Bourse resources surfaced in other nations, though League, Freeborn and some other traders defended the auction. At the Winter Solstice three mandates were upheld, one with a Greater Majority. The General Assembly sent Bartimaeus to urge citizens to strengthen their nations. Raziel of the Shattered Tower urged the Highborn, and Edna of the Chantry urged the prosperous, to shun the Public Auction until the Exchange is built.

n.Highguard: Highborn holding white granite were urged by Raziel of the Shattered Tower to refuse the Bourse auction at Anvil until the Cinderpath Exchange is built, reflecting their national scepticism of the 'invisible hand' of the market.
n.Navarr: Some Navarr brokers resent that only one of the three great weirwood forests in their lands is in Navarr hands, though other Navarr traders are content with their auction profits.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the nations, 'from Wintermark to Urizen', where traders question sending Bourse resources to Anvil.
n.Varushka: Varushkan merchant families nurse a centuries-old jealousy that some Bourse seats in Varushka are not in Varushkan hands, while some Varushkan mine owners are happy with their auction profits; Varushka's white granite is noted as the Empire's finest.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the nations, 'from Wintermark to Urizen', where traders question sending Bourse resources to Anvil.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the proposed palaces of the cardinals in Bastion are listed among the building projects driving demand for white granite.
t.Casinea: Casinea's quarries and mines are one of Highguard's steady sources of white granite, and the territory was the intended home of the Cinderpath Exchange.
t.Reikos: Reikos's quarries and mines produce a steady stream of the white granite that Highborn are now urged to withhold from the Anvil auction.

r.Casinea/Mareholm: The hills of Mareholm were the proposed site of the Cinderpath Exchange, which the Senate has twice declined to build despite the Synod's support.

Nothing great without cost.d: Writing from Holfried, Lisabetta announced that four foreign powers would join a Liberty Pact meeting at Anvil next summit, pursuing the liberation of slaves across Creation. Invoking 'no new fronts', she set out the Empire's priorities: fighting the Jotun without extreme measures to keep diplomacy possible, exterminating the Druj alongside a new Thule military alliance, keeping faith with Highborn pilgrims and Navarr against the vallorn, and confronting the Grendel. She revealed a maritime expedition of private fleets and forces heading for the Grendel homeland, and fortifications on the south coast needing at least five more seasons. She also pledged to speak more with citizens at Anvil.

n.Druj: The Imperatrix declared the Druj a scourge to be eliminated by exterminating the evil of their society, using whatever measures the Empire can muster, including the new Thule alliance.
n.Grendel: With diplomacy having failed, the Imperatrix revealed a great maritime expedition of private fleets and military forces sailing south to prove the Grendel homeland is not safe across the ocean, alongside south-coast fortifications against their raids.
n.Highguard: The Imperatrix pledged to keep faith with the Highborn pilgrims newly walking the trods and with those who agreed to share prosperity so the cost of the vallorn fight is not borne by Highguard alone.
n.Jotun: The Imperatrix expected the Jotun war to rage for long years, but urged it be fought without extreme measures so that Jotun notions of honour are respected and future diplomacy remains possible.
n.Navarr: The Imperatrix praised the Navarr who have stayed their weapons against the vallorn so that the Empire can strike more surely together when the opportunity returns.
n.The League: The League Imperatrix wrote from her guildhouse in Holfried, framing her message around the League saying 'nothing great, without cost' and the legacy of Emperor Frederick.
n.Thule: The Imperatrix announced a new military alliance with the Thule against the Druj, sealed with the Empire's commitment not to abandon its allies to fight alone for as long as it takes.

t.Holberg: The Imperatrix described Holberg flourishing again, protected by white granite and invested coin, regaining the prosperity forfeited under Empress Giselle.

r.Holberg/Holfried: The address was written from the highest window of Lisabetta's guildhouse in the heart of Holfried, looking towards the horizon Emperor Frederick once beheld.

Nowhere and everywhere.d: Irra Harah tersely offered the Spring Archmage alone a parley at 10pm on Friday. Basileus Flint offered the Autumn Archmage, Marcus of Endsmeet, Adelina of Felix's Watch and one other a formal parley with his Vizier. Topics were the Druj relationship with the eternals, Druj armies, maps of Druj territory and help finding and setting spies. Flint also asked for a dose of lethal poison, and any agreement would bind the Empire. Phaleron granted Gralka a parley on the archive and the Anvil library. Wise Rangara offered a meeting, not a parley, on poison. Lashonar set its own agenda for the Archmage of Night, and Rhianos praised the Dubhtraig raid.

n.Druj: The Druj were the subject of Basileus Flint's parley, which offered the Empire information on their dealings with the eternals and on their armies. It also opened discussion of maps of Druj territory.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Night invited to Lashonar's parley is Elyssiathain of Urizen.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wise Rangara's offer of a meeting was addressed to the Winter Archmage, Syn Truth-Walker Returned, who was asked to bring six Academy students.

t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is not named on the page, and none of the arranged parleys or meetings is said to take place there.

Protect or punish.d: Navarr warbands had slowed the vallorn, but three husk swarms, lured by heralds of Yaw'nagrah and guarded by ettercaps, still roamed Brocéliande, and a Navarr party was trapped at Highborn Rest Wayfort. Orc bandits in Willstone had enslaved pilgrims bound for the Conservatory of Music. Druj ambushers and a miasma pillar lurked in the Webwood, where captured scouts were held. Chikad slavers were marching Urizen captives from Caeli towards Zenith. Conjunctions to Stark and East Floes offered a small advantage against the Jotun if taken that season. The Silent Bell found that the Eater-of-Hope's last anchor might lie in Estmure.

n.Dawn: Dawn's region of Estmure was beset by twisted knights, war-witches and yeofolk, possibly through the Eater-of-Hope's final anchor. Its soldiers had also been vanishing in the woods of Ossium.
n.Druj: Druj ambushers, saboteurs and a miasma pillar in the Webwood, and Chikad slavers driving captives out of Caeli, were all targets for Imperial strikes through the Sentinel Gate.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel warlord had been the Eater-of-Hope's anchor, defeated and exorcised in the Summer battle in Spiral.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the trapped Navarr party was heading for Casinea, and Highguard heroes were among those urged to help free captives in Morrow.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Jotun scouts were patrolling the border with Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Jotun skirmishers at Bleak Rise in Stark and on the Sundered Plain in East Floes faced Imperial strikes meant to weaken their hold on those regions.
n.Navarr: Navarr warbands had slowed the vallorn in Brocéliande. Some of their fighters were now trapped in Vale's Lament, and three herald-led husk swarms remained to be struck.
n.The Marches: Marcher beaters fed reports to the prognosticators. Victory at Bleak Rise would help forward units of the Bounders against the Jotun, whose scouts patrolled the Bregasland border.
n.Urizen: Urizen faced pilgrims enslaved by bandits in Willstone and citizens dragged off by Druj slavers in Caeli. Menos urged all ten nations to help free the captives.
n.Varushka: Varushkan soldiers had vanished in the Webwood, where the Golden Axe had recently passed by Fang Tree. Varushkan heroes were also urged to help rescue captives in Morrow.
n.Wintermark: Suaq hunters scouted Jotun movements as the Empire pushed into Sealtoq, and strikes in Stark and East Floes offered help towards retaking more of Sermersuaq.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Jotun scouts were patrolling its border with Sermersuaq.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn had been slowed but not defeated. Four conjunctions opened to rescue trapped Navarr and attack three husk swarms led by heralds of Yaw'nagrah.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the trapped Navarr party had been heading to Casinea, and Vale's Lament lies near its region of Mareholm.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is not named; the page only notes that without a beachhead it would be hard to cross from West March into Stark.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Jotun scouts were patrolling its border with Sermersuaq.
t.Morrow: As Imperial forces advanced, Druj slavers were driving Urizen captives towards Zenith. Two conjunctions into Caeli offered chances to rescue them.
t.Ossium: Despite the Imperial conquest of the Webwood, Druj ambushers and servants of Arhallogen remained there, and two conjunctions offered strikes against them.
t.Redoubt: Orc bandits had grown bold amid the Druj war and enslaved a pilgrimage to the Conservatory of Music. Four conjunctions offered a chance to free the pilgrims.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Exile Trod conjunction lay close to the Llofir-claimed woods of Tamarbode.
t.Semmerholm: Estmure suffered acts of cruelty and murder that the Silent Bell traced to the Eater-of-Hope's possible last anchor, and a conjunction opened to a tortured glade there.
t.Sermersuaq: With a beachhead forced in Sealtoq, conjunctions to Stark and East Floes offered chances to counter Jotun warbands and prepare future advances.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Jotun scouts were patrolling its border with Sermersuaq.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Solstice battle against the Eater-of-Hope's Grendel anchor had been fought there.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Druj slavers were leading Urizen captives along tracks from Caeli towards Zenith, which the Druj had invaded.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Navarr efforts had stopped the vallorn gathering strength here. A conjunction to West Weaver Wood, near the Semmerholm border, allowed an attack on one herald-led swarm.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: A conjunction to the Exile Trod allowed an assault on the third herald of Yaw'nagrah moving through the region with its husks and ettercaps.
r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: In this miasma-drowned region a Navarr party was trapped at Highborn Rest Wayfort, and a second conjunction targeted a herald in the Depths of Lament.
r.Casinea/Mareholm: Mentioned in passing: Highborn Rest Wayfort lay close to the border with Mareholm.
r.Morrow/Caeli: Chikad skirmishers were leading Urizen captives out of the region. Conjunctions to the Meadow of Sighs and Derontian Field offered a race to rescue them.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Druj ambushers and a hidden temple of the Spider King troubled the region. Conjunctions offered a chance to destroy a miasma pillar at Fang Tree and rescue captured scouts at Dark Bark Glade.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: Bandits had enslaved pilgrims bound for the Conservatory at Willstone Spire. Four conjunctions offered light-resistance fights to free them so they could finish their journey.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Mentioned in passing: the Exile Trod in Elerael lay close to the Llofir-claimed woods of Tamarbode.
r.Semmerholm/Estmure: A dreadful shadow fell over Estmure as knights, war-witches and yeofolk were twisted to cruelty, likely by the Eater-of-Hope's last anchor. A conjunction opened to a tortured glade.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: A conjunction to the Sundered Plain offered a chance to overcome Jotun raiders near the Red Wind Corsairs, giving a small advantage towards seizing the region.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Imperial forces had pushed the Jotun back and begun forcing a beachhead here to support the wider campaign in Sermersuaq.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: A conjunction to Bleak Rise offered a chance to overcome Jotun skirmishers near the Bounders' forward units, giving a small advantage towards seizing the region.

Ratify treaty with the Iron Confederacy.d: Proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by Segura, the motion passed in Winter 382YE. The treaty committed the Empire to provide copies of maps of the Bay of Catazar showing all Iron Confederacy and Grendel lands, at a cost of 10 Thrones from the Imperial treasury. The Imperatrix donated 10 Thrones to cover this. The treaty also changed Imperial law: all sale or gifting of liao to the Iron Confederacy, whether through ports or across the Suranni-Imperial border, was banned, making such trades by Imperial citizens illegal.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the maps handed to the Iron Confederacy show all Grendel lands in the Bay of Catazar.

t.Bay of Catazar: Under the treaty, the Empire gave the Iron Confederacy copies of its maps of the Bay of Catazar, showing all Iron Confederacy and Grendel lands there.

Recognise Sand Fishers as foreigners.d: The Sand Fishers are a tribe of orcs living in Ossium who had until recently been subjects of the Druj. The motion, proposed by Miekarova and seconded by Therunin, declared those Sand Fishers who wished to remain part of their tribe to be foreigners. It passed. As a result the Sand Fishers became foreigners in Imperial eyes, receiving the protection of Imperial law for as long as they abide by it. The page notes that the further implications of this recognition were uncertain.

n.Druj: The Sand Fishers, an orc tribe of Ossium who had until recently been Druj subjects, were recognised by the Senate as foreigners, distinguishing them from the Druj enemy.

t.Ossium: The Sand Fishers living in Ossium who wish to remain part of their tribe were declared foreigners, protected by Imperial law so long as they abide by it.

Research Sungold Pass.d: Announced by the Minister of Historical Research, this action commissioned historical research into the history of the Sungold Pass mine. The page notes that the Thule were laying claim to the mine, which lies on the boundary of Otkodov in the eastern foothills of Opascari. The page records only that the research was commissioned; it gives no findings or outcome of the investigation.

n.Thule: The research examined the history of a mine the Thule were claiming, which could bear on the strength of their claim to Sungold Pass.

t.Otkodov: The Sungold Pass mine under research lies on the boundary of Otkodov in the eastern foothills of Opascari, held by Thule at the time.

Rope and iron.d: The Senate gave ambassadorial authority for the summit to Ianthe Ravenswatch, its own appointee, and Eska Crowspeaker, appointed by the Synod. The Constitutional Court ruled that both had to agree any treaty before it could be ratified. The civil service warned that trade with six slaving nations (Axos, Faraden, the Iron Confederacy, the Thule, Jarm and Asavea) could be harmed, which might affect many trade-based commissions. The Fellowship of Purple Sails split over embargoes. The Liberty Pact was signed by the Empire, Sumaah, the Commonwealth and Axos, with the Delves supporting it without signing. It treats hylje and daeva as persons, defines slavery and calls for trade sanctions against slaving nations.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn captain Olivia i Farad i Riqueza co-leads the larger Purple Sails faction. She opposes outright embargoes, warning they would shut Imperial captains out of foreign ports and end any chance of influencing slaving nations.
n.The League: Lucia Sanguineo di Tassato was invited to attend the summit. The League captain Therese di Sarvos led the Purple Sails faction warning of disaster if the summit restricted access to ports such as Nemoria or Vezak.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Marches is not named directly, though Marcher-linked trading interests may sit among the commissions listed as potentially affected.
n.Thule: The Thule are named among the six slaving nations with whom Imperial trade might be harmed, and the Thule Embassy is listed as potentially affected. They were not invited, and the resulting Pact calls for trade sanctions against slaving nations.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Tarquinius Ankarian of Urizen was among those Eska Crowspeaker intended to invite to the summit.
n.Wintermark: Eska Crowspeaker planned to invite Atte Arrowtongue of Wintermark to chair the summit, and Thanmir Hrafnar of Wintermark to attend.

t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura is not named directly; any link comes only through Freeborn trading interests that might be affected by sanctions on slaving nations.
t.Tassato: The Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange is listed among the titles that changed trade relations could affect, and Lucia Sanguineo di Tassato was invited to attend the summit.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named directly; its only possible link is through trading commissions listed as potentially affected.

Swords and sorcery.d: Pelleas Thorne's mandate filled the Dawnish armies with zeal, so no Dawnish general could order Give Ground or Cautious Advance until Winter 383YE. If any general took up an opportunity, that ban became permanent for every Dawnish army. The Hounds of Glory could spend 25 wains of mithril to gain indomitable glory, allowing a No Matter the Cost order to seize a named region at heavy cost in casualties. Enthusiastic yeofolk made enlarging the Golden Sun cheaper, at 100 wains and 200 crowns. Eastern Sky enchanters negotiated a proposed Tower of the East at the Semmerstones, costing 75 wains, to make that army favoured by Summer eternals. The Senate approved the Golden Sun's enlargement, and the Hounds' general paid for indomitable glory.

n.Dawn: Dawn's armies were given a chance to grow stronger through glory: the Hounds of Glory gained indomitable glory and the Golden Sun's enlargement was approved. Because these opportunities were taken, the page's terms mean no Dawnish army may ever again give ground or advance cautiously.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the foe Dawn drove from Semmerholm and from whom Dawn took Ossium, the victories that sparked this fervour.

t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's surprise crossing of the Semmerlak with Summer eternals' aid to invade and swiftly conquer Ossium is cited as one of the triumphs behind the opportunity.
t.Semmerholm: Dawn drove the Druj out of Semmerholm, and the Semmerstones regio was put forward as the site of the proposed Tower of the East, where Dawnish enchanters and Summer eternals could meet.

The divide between.d: The magistrates ruled that the rebels were still Asaveans, so fighting either side was illegal but trading with the rebels was lawful. A Vigilance mandate began listing Imperial units shipping to Nemoria. Lady Madrianna of the Blue Stones, through the embassy in Sarvos, insisted the revolt was not a slave uprising and urged Imperial support for the Plenum. Terentia, directing the rebels from Maragladia, asked for 50 to 100 wains of mithril or weirwood, to be carried by Sumaah ships. The Purple Sails highlighted lucrative trade at Maragladia and Timor. Franco i Erigo chose not to enact his Synod mandate. The Senate then legalised mercenary service on either side.

n.The Brass Coast: Prominent Freeborn were among those who received Terentia Comasigne's petitions for aid, and the Freeborn priest Franco i Erigo chose not to enact his upheld mandate urging Asavean slaves to join the rebellion.
n.The League: Prominent League citizens received Terentia Comasigne's appeals for help, while the Asavean Embassy in Sarvos lobbied the Senate and leading citizens to back the Plenum instead.

t.Feroz: Had the Senate declared war on Asavea, the white granite trade through the Cavabianca Docks and the temples of Feroz and Nemoria would have ended; the Senate instead chose to allow mercenary service on either side.
t.Sarvos: The Asavean Embassy in Sarvos reached out to the Senate and prominent citizens on Lady Madrianna's behalf, arguing that the uprising was a political betrayal rather than a revolt against slavery.

The mystic, the willful.d: The stars stayed hidden over the Barrens, Zenith and Holberg, strengthening naga secretiveness, while Penumbral Veils covered Urdur and several Imperial territories. Citadels were raised in Hahnmark, Kahraman, Kallavesa and Morrow, and pale wolves from a Winter regio in Altis stirred draughir pack instincts. The Concordium of Pallas sped work on the Coursmouth castle and the Salt Guard and wiped away the damage of the Grendel raid on Quzar. Kaela's gift let Imperial citizens held by the Druj die painlessly. Eleonaris's herald Nezha asked for a mithril monument, but the Senate did not engage. The Conclave declined Sadogua's rings and did not instruct him to share a blight cure with Faraden.

n.Dawn: The stars returned over Semmerholm at the Winter Solstice, and the shores of the Semmerlak were suggested as a possible site for Eleonaris's monument.
n.Druj: The Druj were presumed to be behind the shrouds over the Barrens and Zenith, and the Knights of Glory fought them in Morrow and Ossium. Kaela's gift now denies them the corpses of Imperial captives.
n.Grendel: Urizeni Autumn magic wiped away every trace of the Grendel raid on the port of Quzar, and the Knights of Glory refused to fight in Spiral, which Grendel partly held.
n.Highguard: Urizeni magic doubled the pace of work on the new castle at Coursmouth in Necropolis, and the shroud over Necropolis faded away.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Ancestor's Heralds coven raised one of Cathan Canae's castles of stone and ice in the Northspires of Hahnmark, and Krampus stirred in western Skarsind, due to visit Anvil on the Friday night.
n.Jotun: A Navarr citadel was raised over Serra Damata as a sentinel against a possible Jotun return, and the Knights of Glory fought the Jotun in Sermersuaq.
n.Navarr: The Eternal Family raised a citadel to guard Serra Damata in Kahraman, and Revel, the herald of the Lord of the Crossroads, planned to seek their hospitality or that of the Bitterbark Teahouse.
n.The Brass Coast: Madruga and Feroz stayed under Penumbral Veils, a Navarr citadel guarded Kahraman, and Quzar was fully restored after the Grendel raid.
n.The League: The stars vanished over Holberg after the Autumn Equinox, Sarvos and Temeschwar remained veiled, and the League bravos known as the Cuore di Pietra were favoured with Callidus's Tontine tokens.
n.Thule: A Penumbral Veil hung over Urdur in Otkodov, and it was unclear whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi were also shrouded.
n.Urizen: The Spire of the Auric Horizon turned the Canterspire into a crystal fortress, and the Concordium of Pallas sped castle-building and restored Quzar. Morrow remained veiled and was roamed by winter wolves.
n.Wintermark: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of fog and shadow in Kallavesa, and Kallavesi mystics planned to take Goosewhisper Infusion on the Friday evening. The Knights of Glory fought the Jotun in Sermersuaq.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat was not singled out by any of the season's enchantments or eternal messages.
t.Feroz: Feroz remained under a Penumbral Veil, with dark fog and warped stars, expected to fade shortly before the Summer Solstice.
t.Hahnmark: A frozen castle of Cathan Canae stood in the Northspires until the Winter Solstice, and northern Hahnmark was suggested as a site for Eleonaris's monument.
t.Holberg: The stars over Holberg winked out after the Autumn Equinox under a potent shroud, which impeded scrying and heightened naga secretiveness.
t.Kahraman: The Eternal Family of Navarr raised a citadel over Serra Damata to guard against a possible Jotun return.
t.Kallavesa: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a castle of fog and shadow in its marshes, and Kallavesi mystics planned a Friday-night visionary gathering.
t.Madruga: Madruga's Penumbral Veil was expected to fade before the Spring Equinox, and Quzar in Lightsea was fully restored after the Grendel raid.
t.Morrow: The Canterspire became a crystal fortress through Phaleron's power, the territory remained veiled, giant wolves ranged from Altis, and the Knights of Glory fought the Druj there.
t.Necropolis: The shroud over Necropolis faded, and Autumn magic sped construction of the new castle at Coursmouth.
t.Ossium: The Knights of Glory fought the Druj in Ossium this season.
t.Otkodov: A Penumbral Veil hung over Urdur, and it was unclear without scrying whether the rest of Otkodov was also shrouded.
t.Redoubt: The shroud that had hung over Redoubt faded away.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos remained under a Penumbral Veil expected to fade shortly before the Spring Equinox.
t.Semmerholm: After a year of empty night skies, the stars over Semmerholm gradually returned as the Winter Solstice approached.
t.Sermersuaq: The Knights of Glory fought the Jotun in Sermersuaq this season.
t.Skarsind: Krampus stirred from its cold house of bones in western Skarsind, set to visit Anvil on Friday night.
t.Spiral: The Knights of Glory refused to fight anywhere in Spiral after being exposed to the horror at the heart of Screed.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar remained under a Penumbral Veil expected to fade shortly before the Summer Solstice.
t.The Barrens: The stars remained hidden over the Barrens, probably under a recast shroud. Naga there grew more secretive, and Kaela's gift extended into the territory.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: Nezha suggested the shores of the Semmerlak as a possible site for a monument to Eleonaris.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Penumbral Veil also lay over Verthandi.
t.Zenith: The stars over Zenith stayed hidden, and that shroud was expected to fade at the Spring Equinox 383YE but likely to be recast. Kaela's gift reached into the territory.

r.Hahnmark/Northspires: The Ancestor's Heralds called forth one of Cathan Canae's frozen castles of stone and ice here to protect the land until the Winter Solstice.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: A Navarr citadel was raised to stand guard over Serra Damata against a possible Jotun return.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Urizeni Autumn magic helped repair the port of Quzar until every sign of the Grendel raid was gone.
r.Morrow/Altis: Giant, intelligent white wolves emerged from the Regio of the Hound, guarding it and ranging across Morrow by night.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Autumn magic from the Concordium of Pallas let labourers at the new Coursmouth castle achieve six months' work in three.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Penumbral Veil also lay over Nithoggir.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Penumbral Veil also lay over Sküld.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: A Penumbral Veil hung over Urdur, interfering with magical scrying.
r.Spiral/Screed: The horror lurking at the heart of Screed is why the Knights of Glory will not fight in Spiral.

The path that winds.d: A curse of Naeve's Twisting Blight rotted harvests and spread sickness across Morrow, Redoubt and Spiral. The Druj anchored a miasma of despair over Zenith, and sentinels and Highborn soldiers proposed a stealthy rescue raid for the coming season. The Illuminated Circle of Bloodsilver Twilight proposed a 40-wain mithril Block in Cinion to protect Spiral's spires from the Black Plateau, which the Senate commissioned. Fausta of the Arbiter's Seat prepared an arcane projection to seal Morrow's passes, and Tulley of Elos prepared two Day rituals offering hope, but neither was used. Sadogua and Janon offered boons to magicians fighting the Druj.

n.Dawn: Tulley of Elos prepared a ritual to send a message of hope to every Dawnish citizen, fearing those enslaved in the Barrens would take Kaela's gift, but it was never performed; Dawnish magicians were also offered Sadogua's mana boon.
n.Druj: The Druj anchored a miasma of despair over Zenith to break their Urizen prisoners, and faced a proposed rescue raid on their captives and an unused ritual that could have trapped their forces in Morrow.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel armada anchored off Sarvos threatens Redoubt, and the earlier Grendel invasion is blamed for Spiral's lost peace.
n.Highguard: Highborn aid helped keep Morrow's refugees from starving, and a successful raid into Zenith could have freed captured soldiers of the Valiant Pegasus, Granite Pillar and Seventh Wave.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Fausta's unused projection would have sealed the passes between Morrow and Navarr's Therunin.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast is named as perhaps the only nation more vulnerable than Urizen.
n.The League: League magicians were among those offered Sadogua's boon of extra personal mana at the Winter Solstice for fighting the Druj.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: peace with the Thule is noted as having been secured.
n.Urizen: Urizen suffered a starving curse across its territories while being offered a rescue raid into Zenith, the Spiral Block, a pass-collapsing ritual, messages of hope and eternal boons; only the Block was commissioned.
n.Varushka: Varushkan magicians were among those offered Sadogua's boon of extra personal mana for the Winter Solstice.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page; its only link is the Highborn support for Urizen described.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named; the page only notes the Brass Coast's vulnerability.
t.Morrow: Morrow's refugees suffered the blight curse and survived on Highborn and Marcher food, and Fausta's projection to seal its passes against invaders went uncast, leaving them open.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the despairing oppression met during the conquest of Ossium is compared to Zenith's miasma.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt, the only Urizen territory fully in Imperial hands, was struck by the blight curse and threatened by the Grendel armada, and would gain tax and refugees from any successful Zenith rescue.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the oppression encountered during Reikos's liberation is compared to Zenith's miasma.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel armada lies anchored off Sarvos, threatening Redoubt.
t.Spiral: Spiral, still blighted by the Black Plateau and the curse, saw the Senate commission a mithril Block to shield its spires and lift production penalties on mana sites, congregations, herb gardens, mines and forests.
t.Therunin: Fausta's projection would have sealed the passes between Therunin and Morrow to campaign armies, but it was not cast and they remain open.
t.Zenith: A Druj miasma of despair settled over Zenith, and sentinels and Highborn soldiers proposed a stealthy raid from Spiral to free Urizen captives during the following season.

r.Casinea/Casfall: Mentioned in passing: Casfall is not named on the page.
r.Morrow/Caeli: Mentioned in passing: Caeli is not named individually, sharing only in Morrow's general plight.
r.Morrow/Operus: Had Morrow's passes been collapsed, the river crossing at Operus would have been the only route for campaign armies between Morrow and Redoubt.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Fausta's projection would have drawn on Peregro's volcanic hot springs, shaking the region into hills, but it was never cast.
r.Redoubt/Limus: Limus's southern riverbank, guarded by the fortified town of Cargo, would have held the sole remaining crossing from Morrow had the passes been sealed.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Mentioned in passing: orcs still technically control Apulus, though it is unclear who they now are.
r.Spiral/Cinion: The Block commissioned by the Senate will be built in Cinion, harnessing the Winter regio of a blasted grove to protect Spiral's spires.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Mentioned in passing: a summary names the bridge between Operus and Iteri as the remaining route had Morrow's passes been sealed, though the main text places it towards Limus.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: Proceris is not named, sharing only in Zenith's general fate under the Druj.

Unleashing the storm.d: Two maimed former gladiators freed at Dubhtraig, and an Axou captain forced into Siroc by dolphins, revealed that Beoraidh's coliseum holds hundreds of slaves, trains Grendel armies and is guarded by a white granite fortification one season from completion. The eternal Rhianos, invited by the Archmage of Summer, admitted arranging both encounters and eased Golden Voyage for captains sworn to attack Beoraidh. The civil service warned there was little loot to take, but that equal numbers of fleets and soldiers could free up to 2,000 or more slaves, wreck the fortification and destroy the arena. Enough freed fighters could let the Imperial Orcs raise a third army. The outcome was left to the Spring Equinox.

n.Grendel: The Grendel faced a possible raid on Beoraidh that could free thousands of their slaves, destroy their unfinished fortification and coliseum, and hamper the army recruitment they badly need after the Black Plateau. The page also reports rumours that Salt Lady Suriad fell in the Dubhtraig raid.
n.Imperial Orcs: If enough freed gladiators and recruits joined the nation, the Imperial Orcs could raise a third army, provided they secured a second suitable territory. Even fewer recruits would help them replace losses, and the Winter Sun's general could encourage soldiers to go reaving in support of the raid.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsairs uncovered the Axou captain's story, and Freeborn paradors buzzed with brawls over whether the Dubhtraig raid surpassed Erigo's attack on Trivento. Freeborn captains also stood to benefit from Rhianos's help with Golden Voyage.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orc army the Winter Sun was stationed far away in Wintermark's Sermersuaq.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: freed slaves are expected to want a life as far from the Bay of Catazar as they can get.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Axou captain who confirmed the gladiators' story put in at Siroc after dolphins damaged his ship.
t.Mareave: Mareave became the proposed raid target. A successful attack would damage its economy, including the mithril pits at Fundindelf, for at least a year, and destroying the coliseum would stop the Grendel raising an army in the territory.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun was stationed here, and its general could encourage soldiers to support the raid if the army stayed on the defensive.
t.Spiral: Mareave lies south of Spiral, and the civil service warned that a completed Beoraidh fortification would free Grendel armies to attack the Empire in Spiral sooner.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Beoraidh, a poor port sliding into the sea, held a coliseum, slave camps and a half-built white granite fortress. A raid here could free up to 2,000 or more slaves and destroy both structures, though it promised little wealth.

When all the land is in ruins.d: Navarr thorns, one Wintermark captain and Night-woven champions defended Greenstead and Eleri's Stead against miasma, husks, newly cunning ettercaps and heralds of Yaw'nagrah. Small steadings in the vallorn's heart were overrun, and the Broch was besieged. The surge was expected to grow, needing 2,000 to 5,000 force from the Slow the Vallorn action, or Imperial armies, to hold. Options included Dawnish and Highborn mandates, Llofir's aid in exchange for amity and Tamarbode, Tharim's aid at the cost of Navarr herbs and forests, help from the Great Forest orcs, evacuation or a fight to the end. The Dawn and Highguard mandates were enacted. The Conclave rejected Llofir, placing it under enmity, and accepted Tharim's aid.

n.Dawn: Ranae de Rondell enacted the Banners of Rucastle mandate, so Dawnish military units that help slow the vallorn earn extra rewards until the Winter Solstice 383YE.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj presence is given as the reason the route to Boar's Dell from Drycastle is far less feasible.
n.Highguard: Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower enacted the Blade of the Pilgrims mandate. Highborn congregations accept a rank penalty for a year so their faithful add strength against the vallorn in Brocéliande.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the page only compares the ettercaps and the vallorn's past slumber to events in Liathaven, which they hold.
n.Navarr: Navarr thorns and vates bore the brunt of the fighting and held Boar's Dell and Elerael, though steadings in the vallorn's heart fell. The national assembly was offered rival mandates to either evacuate Brocéliande or fight to the bitter end.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a single Wintermark captain, Cadoc Artair Skölsson, joined the defence, and the Kallavesi mystic Tremont of Cundahl presented Llofir's arcane projections to the Conclave.

t.Astolat: Under the enacted Dawnish mandate, noble houses and villages in Astolat are to support Dawnish champions who brave Brocéliande.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn was held back from Boar's Dell and Elerael for the season, but smaller steadings in its heart were overrun, the Broch was besieged, and the surge was expected to intensify.
t.Casinea: Casinea's congregations are called on by the Highborn mandate to send their faithful against the vallorn, at the cost of a rank penalty for a year.
t.Hercynia: Because the Conclave accepted Tharim's aid, Hercynia's herb gardens each lose two random herbs and its forests two resources for a year. It was also named as a possible new home for evacuees.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: its ettercaps and the vallorn's earlier return to slumber there serve as comparisons, and Navarr magicians fighting in Liathaven may also use Tharim's heart's blood boon.
t.Miaren: Miaren's herb gardens and forests pay Tharim's price for his aid. Venomous weapons for the defence came from Honest Twyll's Gardening Supplies there.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: its recent addition to the trod network eases trod-walking, and it was a possible evacuation destination depending on the Senate.
t.Reikos: Reikos is the only practical route for an army to reach Elerael, and its congregations bear the Highborn mandate's penalty. Llofir's garden at Tamarbode lies here.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm offers the only safe route for an army to Boar's Dell. Its knights of Rucastle aided Greenstead, and its people are urged to support Dawnish champions.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: walking the trods through Sermersuaq is noted as difficult.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named; the only related point is that the Druj presence makes an approach via Drycastle much less feasible.
t.Therunin: Therunin's herb gardens and forests pay Tharim's price. The Great Forest orcs sheltering here offered to help but are troubled that the Holt of the Oak commission has lapsed.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: walking the trods through Druj-held Zenith is noted as difficult.

r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: The Broch came under concerted attack by husks and ettercaps and could only survive another season if at least 5,000 force was committed.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Defenders at Greenstead kept the vallorn out of Boar's Dell this season, but the region remains under growing pressure.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Eleri's Stead and Elerael were held this season, though a steading there suffered a vallornspawn attack. Elerael would be the first region lost if fewer than 4,000 force is committed.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: the ruins of Terunael lie at the vallorn's heart, and some of the oldest husks may date from the city's fall.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Llofir, which infests Tamarbode, asked for the region's cession and amity in return for aid. The Conclave refused and placed it under enmity.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Great Forest Encampment of Chief Vallack is here; a Winged Messenger from Therunin's senator could bring his orcs to Brocéliande.

Will you believe?.d: The Sumaah Houses of Virtue declared Timoj the true beacon of the faith and opened it to pilgrims. Their missionaries criticised the Synod over the Temple of Balo in Feroz, the Asavean shrines in Tassato, the Yaelian Schism, orc paragons and ancestor reverence. Proposed responses ranged from refutation and driving the missionaries out to appeasement and excommunicating Sumaah. Doing nothing would cost congregations in Sarvos, Tassato, Redoubt, Spiral and Necropolis 1 liao and 2 votes. Mandates for appeasement, Solas's 'not bound' position, 'Not a Trickle' and 'Hinder Us Not' all failed or were withdrawn. The Synod upheld Jorma's call for common ground, leaving the response to Sumaah, and the missionaries kept preaching.

n.Grendel: Grendel's congregations in Spiral were among those set to lose liao and Synod votes if the Sumaah missionaries went unchecked.
n.Highguard: Bastion's standing as the heart of the Way was directly challenged by Timoj, and orthodox Highborn congregations in Necropolis were judged especially receptive to the missionaries.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr priests were among those favouring appeasement and recognising Sumaah as equal but separate.
n.The Brass Coast: The Sumaah cited the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz as proof of the Synod's laxity, while Freeborn priests were among those urging appeasement.
n.The League: The League's orthodox congregations in Sarvos and Tassato faced losses, the missionaries attacked Tassato's Asavean shrines, and Erasmo di Tassato's appeasement mandate was defeated or withdrawn.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah dismissed 'whatever it is the priests of the Marches preach' as non-doctrinal belief.
n.Urizen: Urizen's sword scholar sympathies made Redoubt's congregations receptive to questioning the Synod, and Solas's mandate denying any fixed heart of the Way failed or was withdrawn.

t.Bastion: The Sumaah urged the faithful to look to Timoj instead of Bastion, and the Synod's chosen mandate cast Timoj as Bastion's counterpart.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: nations along the Bay of Catazar were where the missionaries were expected to erode support for the Synod.
t.Feroz: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz were held up by Sumaah missionaries as examples of the Synod tolerating false religion.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is not named on the page, though Marcher priests' preaching was derided by the Sumaah.
t.Necropolis: Congregations in Necropolis were to provide 1 less liao and 2 fewer Synod votes by the Spring Equinox if nothing were done.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt were to provide 1 less liao and 2 fewer Synod votes by the Spring Equinox if the missionaries went unchecked.
t.Sarvos: Congregations in Sarvos were to provide 1 less liao and 2 fewer Synod votes by the Spring Equinox if nothing were done.
t.Spiral: Congregations in Spiral were to provide 1 less liao and 2 fewer Synod votes by the Spring Equinox if the missionaries went unchecked.
t.Tassato: The Asavean shrines around Tassato were attacked as idolatry, and its congregations faced losing 1 liao and 2 Synod votes each if nothing were done.

Without a plea for mercy.d: A year of Synod debate prompted by Severin's sermon produced many constitutional proposals but no immediate change. Eska Crowspeaker's upheld Wintermark statement led to mandates, raised by Severi Jarlmarison in Wintermark and Rafe in the General Assembly, letting idle priests exchange congregations for military units. Tiana i Zaydan i Riqueza's mandate to boost Freeborn raiders at Beoraidh and open an illegal raid on Kalino's slave camps won a majority, but the Throne's Custodian of Virtue power demanded a greater majority and it failed. Veikko Bondforger's condemnation of Almodin Oktístis left his idolatrous constructions unaddressed. Rykana's recognition as an exemplar of Wisdom has inflamed doubts about orcs in the Way, with dissent expected by Spring.

n.Grendel: The successful raid on Dubhtraig freed Grendel-held slaves, another plan to free slaves from Mareave is underway, and a failed Freeborn mandate would have strengthened units raiding Beoraidh.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn pilgrimage is cited as the source of a penalty on Freeborn units, and Bastion was proposed as the site of grand Cardinals' palaces.
n.Imperial Orcs: The recognition of Skywise Rykana, following Thrace, has brought to a head doubts over whether orcs can be exemplars under the Doctrine of Human Destiny and the law of idolatry, with dissent likely to surface at the Spring Equinox.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly praised the Dubhtraig raid and welcomed the freed slaves, but Tiana's mandate to free more slaves, including those in Kalino, failed after the Throne required a greater majority.
n.The League: A Tassato bishop's refusal to preach on Thrace sets the scene, and Almodin's idolatrous works, including Lorenzo's legacies of virtue and the Great Game casino at Temeschwar, still stand in League lands.
n.Urizen: Urizen is named among the nations where many of Almodin's dubious constructions still stand, and a national statement supporting Veikko could have had local effect.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk is the only Almodin project whose Asavean elements were removed, at great expense.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark assembly backed Eska Crowspeaker's call for idle stormcrows to arm their congregations, and Severi Jarlmarison raised a mandate letting Winterfolk priests exchange congregations for military units at the Spring Equinox.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: one proposal was to build grand palaces for the Cardinals in the city of Bastion as a modern wonder.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Pallas Docks in Cargo are listed among the constructions tainted by Almodin's idolatrous work.
t.Feroz: The failed Freeborn mandate would have let Imperial captains raid across the border from Feroz into Kalino to free slaves.
t.Kalino: The Iron Confederacy's slave camps in Kalino would have been the target of an illegal Spring raid, but the mandate creating that opportunity was not upheld.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk had its Asavean elements removed at great expense, unlike Almodin's other works.
t.Mareave: A plan to free slaves from Mareave is already underway, though the mandate to strengthen Freeborn raiders there failed.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; it is linked only through Urizen, where many of Almodin's idolatrous constructions are said to stand.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: retaking Sermersuaq is cited by Eska Crowspeaker as a virtuous cause for armed congregations to fight for.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the orc preacher who confronts a League bishop over Thrace in the opening story comes from Skarsind.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Spiral Sword runeforge is among Almodin's commissions still bearing idolatrous imagery.
t.Tassato: Tassato is the setting of the opening story, where Bishop Camina is confronted for never preaching on Thrace and dismisses him as irrelevant to humans.
t.Temeschwar: The Great Game casino outside Temeschwar and Lorenzo's legacies of virtue retain Almodin's idolatrous statues and mosaics, with no plan yet to deal with them.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Freeborn units joining the raid on Beoraidh after the Winter Solstice would have gained an extra rank, but the mandate was not upheld.

Years of an inch and a step.d: Kerem's Summer Solstice mandate prompted many young Highborn to sell farms and businesses and take to the trods. At the Autumn Equinox every national assembly urged its citizens to feed, shelter and protect the pilgrims. As a result, every nation's farms and businesses lose 36 rings and its military units one rank for a season, while Highguard's losses stay at 72 rings and two ranks. All these penalties end by the Spring Equinox. The Highborn upheld three non-competing mandates: Shadrach's against false virtues and eternal worshippers, Yarona's casting pilgrims as guides to all human nations, and Dinah's, passed by the greatest majority, urging proselytising to foreigners.

n.Highguard: Highborn farms and businesses keep losing 72 rings and their military units two ranks for one more season before recovering, while the Assembly gave its grey pilgrims a missionary and inquisitorial mission, including a congregation penalty that reaches Highguard itself.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs share the cost of supporting the pilgrims for a season, and Chainbreaker Snark proposed an alternative mandate for the Highborn Assembly urging pilgrims to convert travelling foreigners.
n.Navarr: The grey pilgrims take up part of the burden the Navarr have long carried against the vallorn, though Navarr also pays the season's support penalty and its congregations face the pilgrims' challenge under Yarona's mandate.
n.Urizen: Urizeni citizens reached out to aid the pilgrims and bear a season of reduced income and military strength, and as a human nation their congregations are subject to the one-rank penalty from Yarona's mandate.
n.Varushka: Varushka shares the season-long cost of supporting the pilgrimage, and as a human nation its congregations face a one-rank penalty while grey pilgrims question unorthodox beliefs there.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark bears the season's penalty to farms, businesses and military units for supporting the pilgrims, and its congregations are among those of all human nations hit by Yarona's mandate.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Suranni traders sailing the Bay of Catazar are cited as people the grey pilgrims should tell they worship false gods.
